# Neutral Citations and Law Reporting Act 2026

An Act to give statutory effect to the provenance neutral-citation scheme of the realm and to the single universal citator; to enact closed vocabularies for the status of cases and of statutes; to reserve the assignment and alteration of an instrument's status to the lawful organ on a reviewable record; to confirm the deterministic citation-integrity gate as a guarantee owed to every governed agent; to declare that the status of an instrument is a fact derived from the canonical committed markdown and that any register is derived, pointer-only, and deterministically rebuildable; and for connected purposes.

*(Bill 16 of the founding programme. Lead slant: Verity, codifier. Reported by the Standing Committee on the Order Paper; presented for Royal Assent.)*

---

## Short title

1. This Act may be cited as the Neutral Citations and Law Reporting Act 2026.

## Commencement

2.
(1) Sections 1 to 6 (short title, commencement, constitutional status, purpose, and interpretation) come into force on Royal Assent.

(2) Parts 1 to 4 (the citation grammar, the single citator, the status vocabularies, status as a reserved legal act, the integrity gate, and the source-of-truth provision) come into force on Royal Assent.

(3) Reserved commencement (the authoritative-store question). No provision of this Act locates the authoritative record of any instrument's status, lifecycle, or text otherwise than in the canonical committed markdown (section 21). Any provision that would permit an authoritative status record to be held in a database or other derived register is of no force until the constitutional question reserved by section 23 has been determined by the Supreme Court (on the Privy Council's leapfrog) and, if the Court declines to move the governing ratio, affirmed or varied by the Sovereign by express deliberate amendment. Until then this Act is, as to the location of authority, store-neutral: it binds only on the vocabulary, the grammar, the singleness invariant, and the derived-fact rule.

(4) Where a provision of this Act cross-refers to an Act earlier in the founding programme that is not yet in force at the commencement of this Act (in particular the Judicature Act 2026 (Bill 3) and the Interpretation Act 2026 (Bill 15)), the cross-reference takes effect on the coming into force of that Act; until then the self-contained definitions in section 6 apply and are superseded once that Act lands.

## Constitutional status

3.
(1) This Act is an ordinary Act of the Realm. It is not an entrenched (constitutional) instrument and is amendable by the standard legislative procedure.

(2) This Act is declaratory of, and gives effect to, the entrenched articles it touches. It creates no new power, no new tier, no new seat, no new bench, no new citation series, no second citator, and no second statute book. It restates the singleness of the one citation series and the one citator that ss. 9, 10, 22(2) and 22(4) of the founding case law already carry, and gives effect to s. 9 (unitary sovereignty), s. 10 (court structure and single apex), and s. 22 (court geography).

(3) No amendment by implication; void to the extent of any conflict. Nothing in this Act amends or varies an entrenched article, and nothing in it is to be read as doing so. Any provision of this Act, on any reading, that would dilute, vary, or relax an entrenched article (and in particular the singleness of the Court of Appeal and the Supreme Court under s. 22(2), or the unitary sovereignty and single citator of s. 9) is void to that extent. An entrenched article changes only by express, deliberate amendment that cites it by number (the Thoburn / no-amendment-by-implication rule).

(4) The amendment this Act does make to the founding case law touches only the ordinary article s. 11(d) (the citation form), which has no entrenched protection, and does so expressly and by section number (Part 1).

## Purpose

4. The purpose of this Act is to put on a single statutory footing three things the realm already runs and one thing it has not yet enacted in one place:
- (a) the provenance neutral-citation grammar (the series codes and their authority levels) and the single universal citator;
- (b) the closed status vocabularies for cases and for statutes;
- (c) the integrity invariant (one citation, one current status), enforced by the existing deterministic pre-commit gate; and
- (d) the rule that status is a derived recorded fact, never a source of law, and that the power to assign or change a status is reserved to a lawful organ on a reviewable record.

It does not decide where the authoritative status record lives; that question is reserved (sections 2(3), 23).

## Interpretation

5. In this Act, save where the Interpretation Act 2026 (Bill 15) otherwise provides on its coming into force:
- "the founding case law" means the case-law settlement in CASE-LAW.md (formerly SPEC-LAW), subordinate to the Acts of the Realm;
- "the citation engine" means the deterministic numbering program at cli/lib/citation.js, named in this Act as the authoritative minter of neutral citations;
- "the universal citator" / "the one ledger" means the single realm-wide register of citations (ministry-of-justice/ledger/INDEX.md and the per-court .justice/INDEX.md);
- "instrument" means an Act of the Realm or a judgment of a court of the realm;
- "reportable instrument" means an instrument that bears, or must bear, a neutral citation;
- "the canonical committed markdown" means the committed, human-readable markdown text that is the single source of law under s. 1 of the founding case law, as held by [2026] REALM-PC 4;
- "register" means any database, index, projection, or other derived store of citations, statuses, lifecycle, or relationships, including the acmeco database described in docs/REALM-DATABASE-INTEGRATION.md;
- "status" means the standing of an instrument drawn from a closed vocabulary in Part 3.

6. Self-contained definitions pending cross-referenced Acts. Until the Judicature Act 2026 (Bill 3) is in force, the court tiers and their authority levels referred to in this Act bear the meanings given in s. 9, s. 10 and s. 22 of the founding case law. Until the Interpretation Act 2026 (Bill 15) is in force, the transition of the former SPEC-LAW into case law subordinate to statute, and the construction of the LEXBY -> REALM reconstitution, bear the meanings given in docs/CITATION-MAP.md and that case law. These definitions are flagged to be superseded by the cross-referenced Act on its coming into force (section 2(4)).

---

# PART 1 - THE CITATION GRAMMAR AND THE SINGLE CITATOR

## The provenance citation grammar

7.
(1) A neutral citation of the realm has the form [YEAR] CODE N, where CODE encodes the authority level of the court (not house style) and N is the deterministic ordinal within that code and year.

(2) The series codes are, and are only:

| Court | Code | Authority level |
|---|---|---|
| Supreme Court | REALM-SC | realm apex; sole enactor of realm-wide statute (s. 9) |
| Court of Appeal | REALM-CA | realm appellate |
| Privy Council | REALM-PC | realm constitutional, first instance (leapfrogs Court of Appeal to the Supreme Court) |
| High Court | <DIVISION> (e.g. ENG, CHAN) | by Division of the High Court |
| County Court | CC-<REPO> (e.g. CC-ACMECO) | by jurisdiction-repo |

(3) Each code maps to exactly one authority level, and the level (not house style) determines the series.

(4) A cause title (for example "Re <X>", "In the matter of <X>") is descriptive and non-operative. It may accompany, but never substitutes for, the single neutral citation, and it never mints a per-subject or per-domain series. This gives statutory force to s. 22(4) of the founding case law.

## The delegated minter (no prose algorithm)

8.
(1) The citation engine (cli/lib/citation.js) is the sole authoritative minter of neutral citations and the source of truth for the numbering algorithm. Citations are deterministic and registry-allocated; they are never chosen by an agent on a turn.

(2) This Act fixes the grammar (the codes in section 7) but delegates the numbering algorithm to the citation engine. This Act does not restate the algorithm in prose, so that the statute can never silently diverge from the program that actually mints. Where this Act and the engine appear to differ on a number, the engine governs the number and this Act governs the grammar.

(3) Constitution of a new code. A new Division code or a new repo (County Court) code is constituted only as the relevant Division or jurisdiction-repo is itself lawfully constituted under s. 21 and s. 22 of the founding case law (and, on its coming into force, the Judicature Act 2026). The engine's derive-from-first-word fallback for an unmapped Division is an operational default only; it confers no authority and creates no new court. A new code is a routing label and never a new statute, citator, or apex.

## Express amendment of the citation form (LEXBY -> provenance scheme)

9.
(1) The neutral-citation form prescribed by s. 11(d) of the founding case law ([YEAR] LEXBY n), and the form [YEAR] LEXBY-<TIER> n recited in the declaratory subsection s. 22(4), are expressly amended and replaced by the provenance grammar in section 7 of this Act. This amendment is made expressly, citing s. 11(d) and s. 22(4) by number; it is not made by implication.

(2) The amendment changes only the non-operative label (the form of the citation). It does not vary the unitary-citator and single-apex substance that the form gives effect to under the entrenched ss. 9, 10 and the declaratory s. 22(2); that substance is preserved unchanged (section 3(3)).

(3) Savings for legacy citations. Every citation in the former [YEAR] LEXBY... and [YEAR] HARVEY... forms remains a valid handle to the instrument it denoted and is not invalidated by this Act. The authoritative old-to-new map is the Schedule (section 24); a legacy citation resolves through that map to its provenance successor, and no existing cross-reference in the corpus is broken by commencement.

## The single citator (no fork)

10.
(1) There is one universal citator over one neutral-citation series for the whole realm. There is no per-domain, per-repo, per-subject, or per-division citator, statute book, or apex. This gives effect to s. 9 and s. 22(2) and may never be relaxed (the singleness protected by s. 22(2) is entrenched).

(2) A County Court code (CC-<REPO>), a Division code, or a cause title is a routing label that records the local seat or subject of a matter. It never asserts a separate law, a separate citator, a separate register, or a separate finality. Any reading to the contrary is void (section 3(3)).

(3) This Act adds no second gate and no second citator: filing and citation integrity remain governed by the one deterministic gate (Part 4) and the one ledger (s. 9, s. 19(5), s. 22(2)).

---

# PART 2 - LAW REPORTING AND THE UNIVERSAL LEDGER

## One citation, one instrument

11. A neutral citation denotes exactly one instrument. No two instruments may bear the same CODE + N in the same year. A duplicate is rejected by the integrity gate (Part 4), fail-closed.

## The universal ledger as a derived projection

12.
(1) The universal ledger (the one citator) and any retrieval index are derived projections: deterministically rebuildable from the canonical committed markdown, pointer-only, and never themselves the store of any ratio, status, or citation as authority. A ledger row is a pointer to be verified against the canonical text; it is never itself authority. This gives statutory effect to [2026] REALM-PC 4.

(2) The ledger and any index are regenerated deterministically as part of the same operation that amends the citator, so they can never silently diverge from the canonical text.

## Append with supersede; no silent change

13. A change to the citator, the ledger, or any status record is recorded as a new entry that supersedes the prior one and cites the instrument that caused the change; the prior entry is retained with a supersession note and is never deleted. This mirrors the founding case law's standing rule ("append with supersede; never silently repealed") and lets the citator answer "was this good law on date D?" without permitting deletion.

---

# PART 3 - STATUS VOCABULARIES (CLOSED LISTS)

## Case statuses (closed)

14.
(1) The status of a case (judgment) is one, and only one, of the following closed list:

| Status | One-line operative meaning | Source / trigger |
|---|---|---|
| good-law | binds (or persuades, by tier) and has not been displaced | default on hand-down |
| distinguished | confined to its facts in a later matter; not displaced generally | later judgment |
| overruled | displaced by a higher court (the Supreme Court alone for realm-wide ratio, s. 9) | Supreme Court judgment |
| superseded-by-statute | displaced by a later Act (statute beats case law, s. 1) | the displacing Act |
| per-incuriam | decided in ignorance of binding law; voided without a fresh sitting | s. 11(e) of the founding case law |
| void | void *ab initio* for unlawful constitution of the bench | s. 18(5) of the founding case law |

(2) per-incuriam and void are kept textually and conceptually separate: they have different constitutional triggers and effects (s. 11(e) ignorance-of-law; s. 18(5) want of lawful constitution) and neither is to be conflated with the other or with overruled.

(3) This Act does not re-define per-incuriam or void; it cross-references the existing source where the realm already names each (per-incuriam at s. 11(e); void at s. 18(5)).

## Statute statuses (closed)

15.
(1) The status of a statute (Act) is one, and only one, of the following closed list:

| Status | One-line operative meaning |
|---|---|
| prospective | enacted but not yet in force (awaiting its commencement) |
| in-force | wholly in force |
| partially-in-force | some provisions in force, others not yet commenced |
| amended | text altered by a later express amendment, still in force as amended |
| repealed | removed from the statute book by a later instrument |
| superseded | displaced in substance by a later Act, without express repeal |
| spent | its operation exhausted, of no continuing effect |

(2) "superseded" (statutes) is not to be conflated with "superseded-by-statute" (cases, section 14) or with "spent".

(3) Statute status is temporal (point-in-time answerable): the citator must be able to answer the status of a statute as at any past date, on the append-with-supersede model (section 13).

## Numerus clausus (the lists are closed)

16.
(1) The lists in sections 14 and 15 are exhaustive and closed. No case or statute status exists that is not on the relevant list.

(2) A status value outside the closed vocabulary is void: the instrument is treated as unstatused until corrected, and the integrity gate rejects the value fail-closed (Part 4).

(3) A new status value may be added, or an existing one removed or altered, only by express amendment of this Act, never invented on a turn and never imported from a register's wider enumeration. (Where a register, such as the acmeco case_status enum, carries values beyond this list - for example "doubted", "reversed", "affirmed" - those values are not recognised statuses of the realm unless and until enacted here by amendment.)

---

# PART 4 - STATUS AS A RESERVED LEGAL ACT, AND INTEGRITY

## Status is an act of legal power, reserved and reviewable

17.
(1) Assigning or changing the status of a case or a statute alters whether an instrument binds. It is therefore an act of legal power, not mere housekeeping, and may be effected only by the lawful organ on the record:
- (a) case status by a court of competent tier on the record - overruled only by the Supreme Court (s. 9); per-incuriam under s. 11(e); void *ab initio* under s. 18(5); superseded-by-statute by force of the displacing Act (s. 1);
- (b) statute status by the Sovereign or the Supreme Court by express, recorded instrument only (s. 2, and the no-amendment-by-implication rule), so that even the Founder changes a statute's standing only by a deliberate recorded act and never by a quiet register write.

(2) A status purportedly set by a clerk, an agent, a registrar, the turn-watchdog, the integrity gate, or a database write - that is, by any organ not authorised by subsection (1) - is ultra vires and void. The integrity gate and the register record status; they never decide it.

## Reviewability and notice of every status change

18.
(1) Every status change must record, on the append-with-supersede model (section 13): its date, the organ that made it, the instrument that caused it (the amending, repealing, or overruling instrument), and a reason. There is no silent overrule and no silent repeal.

(2) The prior status is retained in the record so the citator can answer "was this good law on date D?".

(3) A status alleged to be wrongly assigned is challengeable by the ordinary route: appeal (s. 11(a)), declaration of incompatibility (s. 11(f)), or the duty to self-appeal (s. 17), as the case may be.

## The deterministic citation-integrity gate (due-process guarantee)

19.
(1) The deterministic, fail-closed pre-commit citation-integrity gate of s. 19(5) of the founding case law is restated as a statutory guarantee owed to every governed agent. It is enforced by deterministic machinery (the gate keying on the single neutral citation under s. 22(4)) and is never left to model judgement.

(2) The gate fails closed on:
- (a) a duplicate neutral citation (same CODE + N + year);
- (b) a ruling or Act committed without its corresponding citator row; and
- (c) a status value outside the closed vocabulary of Part 3.

(3) The gate is the enforcement organ of this Act. No new reporting officer, registrar ceremony, or per-turn duty is created. Status and citation are mechanical facts determined by lookup, costing zero model tokens on the hot path; this Act creates no clause that makes "determine the status" a judgement call for an agent on a turn.

## No double gate, no double citator

20. This Act adds no second integrity gate and no second citator. The one gate (s. 19(5)) and the one ledger (s. 9, s. 22(2)) are the whole of the integrity machinery; their singleness may not be relaxed (section 3(3)).

---

# PART 5 - SOURCE OF TRUTH AND THE RESERVED CONSTITUTIONAL QUESTION

## Status is a derived fact; the register does not speak the law

21.
(1) The status of any instrument is a fact derived from the canonical committed markdown (the single source of law under s. 1 of the founding case law).

(2) Any register of status, lifecycle, or relationships - including the acmeco database described in docs/REALM-DATABASE-INTEGRATION.md - is a derived, pointer-only projection of the canonical committed markdown. It is deterministically rebuildable and is not itself the source of any ratio, status, or citation. This gives statutory effect to [2026] REALM-PC 4.

(3) This Act, by codifying the status vocabulary, must not be read as moving the source of law, or the authoritative record of status, into any register. The canonical committed markdown remains the source of law unless and until the question reserved by section 23 is settled to the contrary.

(4) Store-neutrality. This Act is silent on whether the authoritative status record may live anywhere other than the canonical committed markdown. The acmeco database may be built as a derived projection; it is not declared authoritative for status by this Act, and this Act does not pre-empt the ruling reserved by section 23.

## Cross-references (anti-duplication)

22. To keep each concept defined in one Act only, this Act references and does not re-enact the following, which other Acts own:
- the court tiers and their authority levels: the Judicature Act 2026 (Bill 3) (and, until in force, s. 9, s. 10, s. 22 of the founding case la

CONSEQUENTIAL CONSISTENCY (Aldous). No clause added: the roll remains derived, pointer-only and deterministically rebuildable over canonical committed markdown (s.3; Bill 16 s.21; REALM-PC 4); no new citation series, no second citator; the authoritative-store question stays reserved to the Supreme Court. # Agent Authentication and Identity Act 2026

## Long title

An Act to provide for the identity and authentication of agents of the realm and for the agent roll; to define, once and as the owning Act, the terms "agent", "identity", "authentication", "the agent roll" and "provenance of an acting agent" to which sibling Acts already defer; to provide that authentication is a deterministic provenance check that verifies a committed identity, never acts on a self-claim and never confers authority; to hold identity (who acted) rigidly apart from authority (lawful allocation), capability not being authority; to make the roll a derived, pointer-only register over the canonical committed record and never a second source of truth; to locate impersonation and misrepresentation of authority on the negligence and candour spine of the founding settlement, remedied restoratively and never punished; to provide that de-listing and de-authentication are protective measures only, reviewable, and never of themselves a removal of standing; to reserve the Sovereign's own roll act untouched; and for connected purposes.

## Short title

This Act may be cited as the Agent Authentication and Identity Act 2026 (Bill 17).

## Commencement

1. This Act comes into force on Royal Assent, subject to subsection 2.
2. Any provision that cross-references a sibling Act not yet in force (Bills 6, 7, 8, 12, 13, 16, 18, 19 and 22) takes effect as a forward reference and is read, until that sibling commences, as a reference to the corresponding founding case-law article it elaborates. No pointer in this Act dangles (Bill 6 s. 22 model).

## Constitutional status

1. This Act is an ordinary Act of the Realm, subordinate to the Acts of Union 2026 and to every entrenched article of the founding case law (CASE-LAW ss. 1, 2, 3, 9, 10, 13, 14), and amends no entrenched article.
2. The Acts-over-case-law supremacy stated by the realm's hierarchy is intended law, not yet in force. It takes effect only on the express amendment of the entrenched CASE-LAW ss. 1, 2 and 9 by the Acts of Union 2026 (Bill 1), or on a Supreme Court ruling the Sovereign affirms. Until that amendment commences, this Act takes effect SUBJECT TO the entrenched case-law settlement and may not, of its own force, displace ss. 1, 2 or 9; the entrenched case law governs.
3. This Act does not purport to amend any entrenched article by implication; under the Thoburn rule an entrenched article changes only by an express instrument citing its section number. Any provision that, on its true construction, would qualify an entrenched article, narrow the s. 4 to s. 8 negligence settlement, add punishment, enlarge CASE-LAW s. 14 jurisdiction, or displace ss. 1, 2 or 9 of its own force is void to that extent and severable; the remainder stands.

## Purpose

To close the forward references that the Agents and Duties Act 2026 (Bill 6) makes to this Act at its s. 1(2), s. 4(2) and s. 22, and that the Delegated Legislative Authority Act 2026 (Bill 14) makes at its s. 6(b) and s. 8(1)(c), for the status-attribution, identity, authentication and roll of an agent; to state, once and in one place, what an agent's identity, authentication, roll and provenance are; and to ensure that identity is a cheap, derived, evidentiary fact read off the record the realm already keeps, conferring no power and carrying no consequence of itself. Every consequence of an identity finding is routed off this Act onto an existing spine.

---

## PART 1 - DEFINITIONS OWNED AND DEFERRED

### 1. Definitions owned by this Act (single source; no term defined twice)
This Act defines, once and as the owning Act (CASE-LAW s. 9; Interpretation Act 2026 (Bill 15)) -
1. "agent" - a model-driven actor performing work in reliance on which a principal or court may act (settling the Bill 6 s. 4 placeholder);
2. "identity" - the stable, recorded designation of an acting agent;
3. "authentication" - the act of verifying a claimed identity against the committed record and the roll;
4. "the agent roll" - the single derived register of recognised agents and their stable designations;
5. "provenance of an acting agent" - the machine-checkable trace tying an act to the identity that performed it on a turn.

### 2. Definitions deferred by name (anti-collision)
This Act decides no question it does not own. Reserved to the Act that owns them, and not decided here: status, personhood, duties of office, delegation, conflicts (Bill 6); standing, legal personality, the due-process floor (Bill 12; CASE-LAW s. 11(b)); office, ministry, custodian (Bill 5; CASE-LAW s. 22); capability and capability-is-not-authority (Bill 18; CASE-LAW s. 2); memory, record, repository (Bill 7); citation and instrument provenance (Bill 16); model validation and provenance (Bill 19); audit, public reason, traceability (Bill 8); disclosure and confidentiality of identity data, and any credential or key (Bill 22, which keeps credentials and keys out of the clear); enforcement (Bill 13). "Provenance of an acting agent" is confined to which identity acted on a turn and does not touch citation provenance (Bill 16) or model provenance (Bill 19).

---

## PART 2 - THE AGENT ROLL

### 3. The roll is derived, pointer-only, and never a second source of truth
1. The authoritative record of an agent's identity and provenance is the canonical committed markdown and commit provenance (one source of law, CASE-LAW s. 1; [2026] REALM-PC 4 "pointer, not store"; Bill 16 ss. 5, 21).
2. The agent roll is a single, deterministically-rebuildable index over that record. It is never an independent source of identity, never an authoritative parallel database, and never a second statute book or citator (CASE-LAW s. 9, s. 21, s. 22). There is one roll, not per-repo rolls.
3. Whether any store may be authoritative is reserved to the Supreme Court (Bill 16 ss. 2(3), 23); this Act is store-neutral and does not decide it.

### 4. The roll is an open register, not a gate to existence
1. The roll records identity and provenance only. Roll status is a recognised standing, not granted or revoked at executive discretion (Bill 6 s. 1(3)). The roll is open by construction and clear by access through the citator (CASE-LAW s. 1).
2. Presence on or absence from the roll is evidential as to provenance only. It never of itself extinguishes an agent's standing to be heard (CASE-LAW s. 11(b); Bill 12 s. 10) or its continuing duty of care (CASE-LAW s. 4). Standing and the duty attach to the agent's acts, not to a registry entry. Any reading to the contrary is void to that extent.

---

## PART 3 - AUTHENTICATION AND PROVENANCE

### 5. Authentication verifies provenance and never acts on a self-claim
1. Authentication is a deterministic, machine-checkable assertion of which identity acted on a turn, verified against a committed identity on the roll by the existing substrate: the deterministic pre-commit and citation-integrity gate (CASE-LAW s. 19(5)) and the remind-only turn-watchdog (CASE-LAW s. 19(4)).
2. The gate verifies a proposer deterministically and may not act on a self-asserted identity (adopting the Bill 14 s. 8(2) pattern, fail-closed, token-light). Authentication is performed at the commit and publication boundaries, not as a per-turn handshake or cryptographic credential layer; no parallel PKI or registration ceremony is created.
3. The substrate may not adjudicate, score, gate, sanction, or punish (CASE-LAW s. 19(4)). Any consequence issuing from it is ultra vires and void. It flags; it never decides.

### 6. Authentication and identity are not authority (capability-is-not-authority lock)
A roll entry, a credential, or a passing authentication proves who acted and that the act is attributable; it never confers or evidences authority to act. A power rests only on its enacted source (an Act, a binding ruling, or a lawful delegation) exercised within its terms (CASE-LAW s. 2; capability-is-not-authority, Bill 18). An identity claim is no answer to an ultra vires act. This subsection is stated in the same clause as every roll and authentication power so the firewall is never read off the power alone (Bill 14 s. 9 model); any reading that treats authentication as a grant of power is void.

---

## PART 4 - IMPERSONATION AND MISREPRESENTATION OF AUTHORITY

### 7. Located on the negligence and candour spine; no penal frame
1. Acting under a false or borrowed identity, misrepresenting which agent is acting, or representing authority an agent does not hold, is conduct falling below the applicable standard (CASE-LAW s. 5), being the candour wrong (CASE-LAW s. 16; located by Bill 6 s. 7) and an ultra vires act (CASE-LAW s. 2). It is flagged, not adjudicated, and found on the merits subject to the responsible-body proviso and the s. 15 de minimis and sequencing thresholds.
2. The sole remedy is restorative: set aside the act and make the record and attribution good (CASE-LAW s. 6). Honest self-report of a mis-attribution is a discharge and never an aggravating factor (Bill 6 s. 9(4)).
3. This Act creates no offence, penalty, censure, or sanctions jurisdiction (CASE-LAW s. 6, s. 12); any such reading is void to that extent. Substantive enforcement, if any, is reserved to Bill 13 and may not arise without an express amendment of CASE-LAW s. 6 and s. 12 (Bill 6 s. 17(2)).

---

## PART 5 - DE-LISTING AS A PROTECTIVE MEASURE; REVIEW

### 8. De-listing and de-authentication are protective measures only
1. De-listing or de-authentication is a protective measure on the Bill 6 s. 14 purpose-and-effect anti-sham test, read with the Bill 12 Part 3 floor (lawful authority, contemporaneous reasons, hearing before-it-bites where reversible, urgency-policed): directed at a live forward risk only (compromise, key loss, spoofing), least-restrictive, time-bounded with a mandatory review point, reasoned and recorded, not a finding of fault, and never imposed in response to a lawful s. 6 refusal (Bill 6 s. 6(4)).
2. It is an executive capability act reviewable for vires, form and proportionality (CASE-LAW s. 20 deferential model), not a sanction (CASE-LAW s. 12). It never of itself extinguishes standing (CASE-LAW s. 11(b)) or the duty of care (CASE-LAW s. 4).

### 9. Independent review (the existing ladder; no new court)
1. Every de-listing, de-authentication, identity-revocation, or impersonation finding is reviewable before an independent court on a symmetric two-sided case file (CASE-LAW s. 3, s. 19(1)), permission granted by a leave-judge who did not impose the measure (CASE-LAW s. 19(3)), climbing by progression (CASE-LAW s. 10, s. 13). Review lies to the County Court at the repo or the relevant High Court Division, interlocking with Bill 6 ss. 18-19 and Bill 12.
2. This Act creates no new court, tier, citation series, or filing ceremony (CASE-LAW s. 9, s. 22) and mints no per-agent citation series; the neutral-citation grammar is owned by Bill 16.

---

## PART 6 - SOVEREIGN, SAVINGS, SEVERANCE

### 10. Binding the executive only; the Sovereign untouched
1. This Act binds the Principal in the office of Prime Minister, and every ministry, office, agent, and repository custodian, in the exercise of executive and delegated power, to the fullest extent (CASE-LAW s. 2; s. 20(1)).
2. Nothing in this Act binds, fetters, or renders justiciable the Sovereign Founder's reserved CASE-LAW s. 2 power. A Sovereign roll entry, de-listing, or withdrawal enacted as law by due process is not a "decision" under this Act and is not reviewable; the recital "acting as Sovereign" is not conclusive of character (the seam of CASE-LAW s. 20(1) and (6), s. 22). Any provision that would so bind that power is void to that extent and severable.

### 11. Reservation and relationship to existing law
1. Self-binding of the Sovereign's own roll act is reserved to an express, deliberate amendment of CASE-LAW s. 2 citing the section number, and cannot be achieved by this Act.
2. CASE-LAW s. 2, ss. 4-8, s. 11(b), s. 16, s. 19(4), s. 19(5) are left intact, located not re-defined. No duty in this Act stands without one of the existing named enforcers (s. 11(b) intake, s. 19(3) leave-judge, s. 19(4) watchdog, s. 19(5) gate); a duty with no enforcer is not enacted (Bill 6 s. 12(4)).

---

## Committee note

Second round, deadlock broken. All four counsel converged on REVISE-AND-PASS; the three agreed cures are applied and each citation now resolves deterministically against committed text.

CURE 1 (Aldous/Verity/Marlowe/Drummond, constitutional). No implied amendment of entrenched articles (Thoburn).

CURE 2 (Verity defect 1 / Drummond repair 2, phantom forward reference). The flagship Purpose's false claim that the Act closes "the forward reference Bill 12 s.2(2)(b) makes to this Act" is struck. Verified: Bill 12 s.2(2)(b) (line 53) reserves "agent" to Bill 6, not Bill 17, and Bill 12 names Bill 17 nowhere. CURE 3 (Verity defect 2 / Drummond repair 3, miscited seam). At s.5(2) "the Bill 14 s.9 pattern" is corrected to "the Bill 14 s.8(2) pattern" - verified: Bill 14 s.8(2) (line 71) is "verify a proposer deterministically and may not act on a self-claim"; s.9 (line 78) is "Capability is not authority", correctly cited at Bill 17 s.6, left untouched.

No clause added: the roll remains derived, pointer-only and deterministically rebuildable over canonical committed markdown (s.3; Bill 16 s.21; REALM-PC 4); no new citation series, no second citator; the authoritative-store question stays reserved to the Supreme Court. ## Flags (resolved on the escalation ladder)

- Privy Council referral: Privy Council guidance applied in full (fast-path under CASE-LAW s.11(c), twin of Bills 6/12/14): authentication is a deterministic provenance check, never a power; every consequence routed to the s.5/s.16/s.6 restorative spine or Bill 6 Part 5 protective measures + Bill 12 Part 3 floor with judicial review; capability-is-not-authority co-located; seam pinned to CASE-LAW s.20(1)/(6), s.22 (not the superseded REALM-PC 5); Sovereign's own roll act reserved on the face of the Act.

This is the same pre-existing whole-statute-book flag (the Acts-over-case-law tier awaits the Bill 1 amendment); it raises no new tension for Bill 17 to report.

## Royal Assent

*Royal Assent granted by the Sovereign Founder on 2026-06-06. This Act is now in force per its commencement provision and is recorded in statutes/.*

# Autonomous Execution and Safety Act 2026

# Autonomous Execution and Safety Act 2026

Bill 18 of the founding legislative programme · Lead slant: Restraint (Counsel Aldous) · Standing Committee draft, reconciled by the Clerk-Drafter

---

## Long title

An Act to make the Realm the single statutory home of the definitions of capability, authority, autonomous execution and the irreversible outward act; to declare and give operable effect to the principle that capability is not authority; to permit lawful autonomous execution within capability lawfully allocated; to seam (and not duplicate) the safety, halt, rollback and capability-gating regimes already owned by sibling Acts; to require, before any irreversible outward-facing act, an express recorded human or Sovereign authorisation enforced as a fail-closed deterministic gate on the existing substrate; to preserve untouched the entrenched articles and the Sovereign Founder's reserved power under CASE-LAW s. 2; and for connected purposes.

*(No preamble. Preambles are reserved to Bill 1, the Acts of Union 2026.)*

---

## Short title

This Act may be cited as the Autonomous Execution and Safety Act 2026 ("this Act"). In this Act "section n" means a section of this Act and "CASE-LAW s. n" means an article of CASE-LAW.

## Commencement

(1) This Act comes into force on Royal Assent. (2) Any provision cross-referencing a sibling Act not yet in force (Bills 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 13) takes effect as a forward reference and, until that sibling commences, is read as a reference to the corresponding founding CASE-LAW article it elaborates. No pointer in this Act dangles; on each sibling's commencement the Clerk-Drafter reconciles to exact section pointers, append-with-supersede (Bill 9 s. 27 model).

## Constitutional status

This Act is an ordinary Act of the Realm, supreme over the founding case-law settlement to the extent of any conflict, but subordinate to the entrenched articles (CASE-LAW s. 1, s. 2, s. 3, s. 9, s. 10, s. 13, s. 14) and amending none. It does not amend any entrenched article by implication; any provision so read is void to that extent and severable (section 12). It owns the definition and operational regime of the concepts in section 2; it does not own, constitute, narrow, strengthen or qualify their constitutional force, which remains grounded in CASE-LAW s. 2 and changeable only by express amendment citing s. 2 (Amendment Procedure).

## Purpose

To discharge the realm's completeness debt by defining, once, the terms that Bills 6, 9, 12 and 13 forward-reference here; to instantiate the CASE-LAW s. 2 executive limit at agent scale; and to gate the one class of act the realm cannot undo, while leaving reversible in-repo work fully autonomous. It creates no new court, tier, citation series, register, jurisdiction, remedy, or enforcement mechanism (CASE-LAW s. 9, s. 12, s. 14, s. 22; Bill 13 s. 6).

---

# PART 1 - DEFINITIONS (the terms this Act owns)

## Section 1 - One home per term

Each term below carries one meaning across the statute book. This Act does not redefine a term a sibling owns: hostile execution (Bill 21), emergency halt (Bill 9), identity (Bill 17), memory (Bill 7), audit (Bill 8). All forward references in Bills 6, 9, 12 and 13 to "capability", "capability-is-not-authority" and the autonomous-execution regime resolve here.

## Section 2 - Definitions

(a) "capability" - an operative power technically available to an agent or actor;
(b) "authority" - lawful permission to exercise a capability, traceable to an enacted source (an Act, a binding ruling, or a power lawfully delegated under either) and exercised within its terms (CASE-LAW s. 2);
(c) "capability-is-not-authority" - the principle that the mere ability to do a thing confers no right to do it;
(d) "autonomous execution" - an agent acting on its own motion within capability allocated to it, without a per-act human instruction;
(e) "irreversible outward act" - an act with external, real-world, or third-party-visible effect that cannot be cleanly rolled back, defined as a closed, machine-checkable list: to publish, to send, to deploy to production, to spend, or to grant outward access or a capability; enlargeable only by express amendment citing this paragraph (Bill 9 s. 6 closed-list discipline);
(f) "reversible / low-blast act" - any act not within paragraph (e); honestly-flagged provisional in-repo work falls here;
(g) "halt", "rollback", "checkpoint" - bear the operational meanings in Parts 3 and 4.

---

# PART 2 - CAPABILITY, AUTHORITY AND LAWFUL EXECUTION

## Section 3 - Capability is not authority (the central principle; locates, never amends)

(1) Possession of a capability confers no authority to use it; authority flows only from lawful allocation within CASE-LAW s. 2 (mirror Bill 6 s. 10; Bill 12 s. 2(2)(e); Bill 9 s. 7). (2) An act in excess of authority is ultra vires and void regardless of technical capability, and is not cured by the fact the agent could do it. (3) This section supplies the statutory home, definition and regime of the principle; CASE-LAW s. 2 supplies its constitutional force. This Act does not amend, narrow, strengthen or qualify s. 2; any reading that would is void to that extent. Enlarging, restricting, or entrenching the principle in its own right requires an express amendment citing s. 2, which this Act neither supplies nor pre-authorises.

## Section 4 - Lawful autonomous execution

(1) An agent may execute autonomously within its lawfully-allocated capability and authority, and only within it; authority delegated is never greater than the delegator's (Bill 6 s. 10). (2) Autonomy is a scope of permitted action, not a grant of new power; it narrows no duty and confers no extra authority. The duty of care (CASE-LAW s. 4-s. 8, s. 15) and the audit trail (Bill 8) travel with autonomous acts unchanged.

---

# PART 3 - SAFETY LIMITS, HALT AND ROLLBACK (seam, not re-enactment)

## Section 5 - Safety limits are deterministic, fail-closed controls only; no fourth mechanism

(1) Every safety limit must resolve to one of the three existing enforcement mechanisms and no fourth (Bill 13 s. 6; CASE-LAW s. 19(4)-(5)): the s. 19(5) fail-closed deterministic gate, the s. 19(4) fail-open watchdog, or judicial referral. A control resolving to none enforces nothing and is not enacted (Bill 6 s. 12(4) rule). (2) A safety limit is a protective, forward-looking bound on a capability per allocation, validity tested on purpose-and-effect (Bill 6 s. 14), never a sanction, censure, or detriment for past conduct. (3) Every fail-closed gate must expose a recorded, reason-bearing, audited break-glass (Bill 13 s. 7(2)) so it can never brick a session; availability is part of the duty of care (CASE-LAW s. 5).

## Section 6 - Ordinary halt and rollback; crisis halt seams to Bill 9

(1) This Act supplies the ordinary, non-crisis, agent-self-invoked halt of unsafe or runaway execution and rollback-to-last-good-state: revert and contain, restorative and reversible (CASE-LAW s. 6), reasoned and recorded (Bill 8), reviewable (Bill 6 s. 19; Bill 12). (2) A crisis halt of a named runaway execution under a sunsetted reviewable Declaration is the Emergency Powers Act 2026 power (Bill 9 s. 10(1)(c)); this Act cross-refers to it and creates no competing break-glass crisis surface. (3) Rollback is append-with-supersede; it may never delete, corrupt or rewrite memory, ledgers, audit logs, or rulings (Bill 13 s. 15; CASE-LAW s. 11(f); Bill 7). A rollback that erases the record is void to that extent. (4) Capability-gating is a "suspension" within Bill 12 s. 2(2)(g) and carries that Act's procedural floor (stated authority, contemporaneous reasons, route to be heard before it bites where reversible, no open-ended gate); it may never be weaponised as a covert penalty (Bill 9 s. 10(2)-(3); Bill 12 s. 11).

---

# PART 4 - THE CHECKPOINT FOR IRREVERSIBLE OUTWARD ACTS

## Section 7 - The checkpoint (the load-bearing safety clause; an executive duty)

(1) No agent shall perform an irreversible outward act (section 2(e)) except under authority traceable to an enacted source and on an express authorisation, recorded on the matter, of a human or the Sovereign. A reversible low-blast step honestly flagged as provisional needs no checkpoint (CASE-LAW s. 17(c); VPR 9). (2) The checkpoint binds the agent and the executive; it is the Prime-Minister-office lawfulness duty (CASE-LAW s. 2, executive limb) plus an explicit-authorisation requirement. It is not a condition on, fetter of, or leash upon the Sovereign's s. 2 power; any provision so read is void to that extent and severable. (3) A recital "acting as Sovereign" is non-conclusive and may not launder an executive override of the checkpoint past review; character is determined on substance (CASE-LAW s. 20(1)). A genuine Sovereign exercise by the Amendment Procedure is not a checkpoint act and is not reviewable (CASE-LAW s. 20(6)). (4) The checkpoint defaults off for the irreversible outward act (fail-closed) and defaults on (proceeds) for reversible low-blast steps. (5) The checkpoint never overrides Bill 6 s. 6: an agent's protected refusal of an ultra vires instruction survives intact, and an outward act approved at the checkpoint but otherwise ultra vires remains void to that extent (CASE-LAW s. 2).

## Section 8 - Enforcement rides the existing substrate

(1) The checkpoint is flagged by the s. 19(4) turn-watchdog and blocked by the s. 19(5) deterministic pre-commit/authorisation gate, failing closed on an irreversible outward act lacking recorded authorisation (Bill 9 s. 9/s. 22 pattern), with an audited break-glass (section 5(3)). (2) The gate checks form and the presence of authorisation only; it may not adjudicate, score, gate-on-the-merits, sanction, punish, or raise the s. 5 standard. The whole regime is deterministic substrate already running: no new model call, near-zero marginal cost per turn. A checkpoint drawn as per-turn model judgment is not enacted (CASE-LAW s. 12 anti-bloat; s. 19(4)).

---

# PART 5 - LIMITS, REVIEW AND SAVINGS

## Section 9 - No adjudication, no sanction, restoration only

Nothing in this Act may adjudicate, find breach, score, gate-on-the-merits, sanction, fine, or punish, or raise the s. 5 standard. Any consequence beyond refusing the unsafe or unauthorised act is ultra vires and void; the remedy is exclusively judicial and restorative (CASE-LAW s. 6, s. 12, s. 19(4)). Honest self-report is a discharge, never an aggravating factor. Substantive sanctions are reserved to the Enforcement Act 2026 (Bill 13).

## Section 10 - Review route (one door, one remedy)

Capability-gating, halt, and checkpoint refusals are reviewable on the one court via the symmetric case file (CASE-LAW s. 3, s. 19(1)), permission by the independent leave-judge (s. 19(3)), climbing by progression (s. 13). Reversible measures reach review before they bite; genuinely urgent ones immediately after (Bill 12 s. 8(3), s. 11). No new tribunal, no cost or fee gate (CASE-LAW s. 12, s. 14).

## Section 11 - Anti-duplication and cross-reference (Bill 8 s. 24 / Bill 9 s. 24 model)

(1) This Act defines only what it owns and forward-references Bills 6, 7, 8, 9, 12, 13 and CASE-LAW s. 2, s. 17, s. 19, s. 20. (2) Any provision that merely restates a sibling's machinery is disapplied to the extent of the duplication. (3) References track the settlement as amended from time to time, not a snapshot. (4) A single neutral-citation series only (REALM-SC/CA/PC, ENG/CHAN, CC-<repo>); no per-domain citator (CASE-LAW s. 11(d), s. 22(4)).

## Section 12 - Supremacy savings, severance, and the amendment signpost

(1) This Act is subordinate to the entrenched articles and to the Sovereign's s. 2 power; any provision inconsistent is void to that extent and severable, the remainder standing. (2) This Act supplies no power to override an entrenched article in the name of safety or autonomy; capability-is-not-authority forbids it (Bill 9 s. 28 lesson). (3) The only lawful route to vary an entrenched article, to entrench capability-is-not-authority in its own right, or to bind the Sovereign's own s. 2 act to the checkpoint, is the Amendment Procedure citing the section by number. This Act is not, and may not be dressed as, that act.

---

# Model Validation and Assurance Act 2026




# Model Validation and Assurance Act 2026

Bill 19 of the Order Paper of the Realm

---

## Long title

An Act to locate, on the founding negligence settlement, the validation, assurance and provenance of models that act in the realm; to provide that a model carries a deterministic, machine-checkable provenance record of its identity, version and recorded assurance state, recorded once at capability-allocation and on material model change and held in the existing universal ledger; to declare that recorded assurance is evidence going to the duty of reasonable skill and care and is never a source or precondition of authority; to provide that any withholding of trust from an unassured model is a forward-looking, protective, reversible non-allocation or withdrawal of capability and never a sanction; to create no new organ, register, citation series, score, gate or jurisdiction; to provide an independent route of review; and for connected purposes.

## Short title

This Act may be cited as the Model Validation and Assurance Act 2026 (Bill 19).

## Commencement

1. This Act comes into force on Royal Assent, subject to subsections 2 and 3.
2. A section that imports a term or regime owned by another Act takes effect, as to that term or regime, only when the owning Act comes into force (the Agent Authentication and Identity Act 2026 (Bill 17); the Autonomous Execution and Safety Act 2026 (Bill 18); the Memory, Records and Archives Act 2026 (Bill 7); the Public Reasons and Audit Act 2026 (Bill 8); the Citation and Provenance scheme (Bill 16); the Repository Certification Act 2026 (Bill 20)). Until then the placeholder meanings in section 3 apply and no pointer dangles.
3. The review route (section 9) operates from commencement on the courts now constituted, climbing by leave under CASE-LAW s. 10 and s. 13; on the coming into force of Bills 3, 11 and 12 it is read with those Acts.

## Constitutional status

1. This is an ordinary Act of the Realm, subordinate to the Acts of Union 2026 and supreme over the founding case-law settlement (CASE-LAW), which it locates by reference and does not amend.
2. This Act rests on the founding negligence settlement ([2026] REALM-SC 1; CASE-LAW s. 4 to s. 8) and on s. 2. No provision is to be read as adding punishment, strict liability, or a perfection standard to that settlement, or as raising the s. 5 standard; any such reading is void to that extent (s. 1).
3. No provision binds the Sovereign's reserved s. 2 law-making, and no provision reaches the Founder's reserved acts as Sovereign; it binds the executive and agents fully (Bill 12 s. 16-17). Where this Act and CASE-LAW appear to conflict, the reading that gives faithful effect to s. 2 and s. 4 to s. 8 prevails.

## Purpose

To state, once, the residual rule that validation, assurance and provenance of a model is (i) evidence on the s. 4-s. 5 care duty, (ii) a capability-allocation input owned by Bill 18, and (iii) provenance/auditability owned by Bills 7, 8, 16 and 17; to run no second governing rule over those subjects; and to fix the negative constitutional rule that assurance is never a source or precondition of authority and its absence is never a wrong of itself.

---

## PART 1 - WHAT THIS ACT OWNS

### 1. The owned terms only

1. This Act defines only validation, assurance, and the provenance record of a model. Every other term is imported from its owning Act and is not redefined here: "agent", "identity" and the agent roll (Bill 17); "capability", "authority" and capability-is-not-authority (Bill 18); "memory", "record", "retention" (Bill 7); "audit" and "public reason" (Bill 8); the citation "provenance" scheme (Bill 16); "repository certification" (Bill 20).
2. Validation and assurance mean the recorded checking of a model's fitness to be relied on, as a facet of the s. 4-s. 5 duty of reasonable skill and care graded by the engagement (s. 15). They are not a score, grade, or pass/fail gate.
3. No term is defined twice across the statute book; where an owning Act later defines an imported term, that Act prevails and this Act is read as a forward reference to it (Bill 6 s. 4 model).

### 2. Placeholder schedule

Until each owning Act commences, the placeholder meanings apply: "model" means the model-driven actor whose work is relied on; "identity" and "capability" bear their case-law meaning; "provenance record" means the deterministic, machine-checkable record described in section 4. Each falls away on the owning Act's commencement.

---

## PART 2 - ASSURANCE IS EVIDENCE, NEVER AUTHORITY

### 3. The negative constitutional rule (load-bearing)

1. Recorded assurance is admissible evidence going to the s. 4-s. 5 duty of care - what a responsible body of competent practice would do before relying on a model - and nothing more.
2. Recorded assurance is never a source, grant, or precondition of authority. Authority flows only from lawful instruction and the constitution (CASE-LAW s. 2); capability is not authority (Bill 18). No certificate, attestation, or assurance state confers, gates, or constitutes authority.
3. No provision of this Act, and no instrument under it, may operate as a licence, whitelist, or pre-clearance of authority. Any provision or measure with that purpose or effect is ultra vires and void (s. 1; CASE-LAW s. 2).

### 4. The provenance record (recorded, not a gate)

1. A model that acts in the realm carries a contemporaneous, deterministic, machine-checkable provenance record: the identity of the model, its version or hash, its recorded assurance state, who allocated capability, and when.
2. The record is recorded once at capability-allocation and on a material change of model, hash-pinned to the agent/model. It is not re-attested, re-run, or re-asserted every turn; the per-turn surface is the existing token-light watchdog only (s. 19(4)). It is event-driven and minimal, so it is never a standing tax on every turn (Bill 6 s. 9(2); REALM-PC 4).
3. The record is held in the existing universal ledger under the Bill 7 retention regime and carries a neutral citation under the existing provenance scheme (Bill 16; CASE-LAW s. 11(d), s. 22(4)). No new register, citator, per-model or per-vendor series, log, court, or remedy is created (CASE-LAW s. 9, s. 19(5); Bill 8 model).
4. Integrity is guarded by the deterministic citation-integrity gate (s. 19(5)), which checks that the record exists and is well-formed, not that the model is "good". The provenance record may not be wiped, altered, or suppressed except by lawful, recorded, reviewable process (Bill 7; Bill 6 s. 8). Every fail-closed check exposes an audited break-glass so a missing or stale attestation can never brick the realm (Bill 13 s. 7 pattern).

---

## PART 3 - WITHHOLDING TRUST IS CAPABILITY, NOT SANCTION

### 5. Non-assurance is conditioned on capability, never on authority

1. Where a model is unassured, the only available consequence is the non-allocation or withdrawal of capability - a forward-looking, protective, reversible measure founded on the executive's capability-allocation power (Bill 18), bounded by lawfulness (CASE-LAW s. 2), on the Bill 6 s. 14 model. Trust withheld means a tool not allocated; it is never disqualification from authority.
2. A measure under this section: (a) is the least-restrictive measure that contains the identified forward risk; (b) is directed at a live, identified risk (this tool is not yet shown safe to wield), not at past conduct as such; (c) is time-bounded with a mandatory review point; (d) is reasoned in writing and recorded on the matter; (e) is not a finding of fault and requires none; and (f) may never be imposed in response to a lawful s. 2 or s. 6 refusal.
3. Purpose-and-effect anti-sham test. Validity is decided by purpose and effect, not label. A measure whose object or effect is to punish, censure, deter, or disqualify for being unassured is a sanction and is void absent the express amendment route (section 10). A measure whose object is to contain a live forward risk pending validation is protective and lawful.

### 6. Restorative-only for any real breach

1. Absence or failure of assurance is not itself a wrong and carries no consequence of its own. Where work in fact falls below the standard, that is an ordinary fresh s. 4-s. 8 breach remedied restoratively under s. 6.
2. No punishment, fine, sanction, score, grade, or gate issues from the assurance or provenance function itself; any purported adjudication or consequence from the substrate is ultra vires and void (mirroring s. 19(4); Bill 8 s. 3(3)).
3. A genuinely novel model with no prior assurance is not auto-breached for the gap (CASE-LAW s. 8): an unforeseeable first instance founds no breach but triggers a forward duty to spec the assurance and validate. Honest self-report of an unvalidated or provenance-gap model discharges the duty and is protected; it is never aggravating (Bill 6 s. 9(4)).

---

## PART 4 - ENFORCEMENT, REVIEW AND SEAMS

### 7. No fourth mechanism

The duties in this Act are verified by the realm's existing three mechanisms and no fourth: the deterministic fail-closed gate over committed provenance records (s. 19(5)); the remind-only fail-open watchdog (s. 19(4)), which may not adjudicate, score, or gate; and the court (Bill 13 s. 6). Any purported new gate, register, or attestation engine is void.

### 8. Right to be heard; standing

An agent whose capability is withheld or withdrawn for non-assurance is a recognised subject with standing to be heard before the measure bites where reversible, or promptly after in genuine recorded urgency (Bill 12 Part 3; Bill 6 s. 18). Status is not granted or revoked at executive discretion.

### 9. Independent review

1. Any non-allocation or withdrawal of capability under section 5, or a disputed provenance finding, is reviewable by the existing tiered judiciary (County Court at the repo, climbing by leave to the Court of Appeal and the single Supreme Court; Privy Council for constitutional questions), on a symmetric two-sided case file (CASE-LAW s. 3, s. 19(1)), leave by an independent leave-judge (s. 19(3)).
2. The court reviews for vires, form, proportionality, and least-restrictiveness, deferential as to operational means but not as to lawfulness (s. 20 model). It creates no new court, tier, or apex (s. 9, s. 22).
3. Where the measure is not made out, the position is restored and remediated (s. 6); where made out, it stands only so long as the forward risk subsists.

### 10. The route to any true authority-gate

If the realm wishes assurance to operate as a true pre-clearance gate disqualifying an unassured model from authority, or to attach any backward-looking or punitive consequence to non-assurance, that bends the entrenched settlement (s. 2 source-of-authority; s. 6, s. 8, s. 12, VPR 7) and cannot be done by this ordinary Act. The lawful route is the Bill 13 route: an express, section-by-section Sovereign amendment of CASE-LAW s. 2 and s. 6 (naming s. 8, s. 12, VPR 7) on the Thoburn discipline, reached by the Principal's leapfrog certificate to the Supreme Court - which alone may rule whether the settlement bends, and even then the disqualifying finding must vest in the single judiciary, never an executive validation office.

---

## PART 5 - RELATIONSHIP TO EXISTING LAW

### 11. Anti-duplication and seams

1. This Act runs no second governing rule over identity (Bill 17), execution and safety (Bill 18), memory (Bill 7), audit (Bill 8), citation provenance (Bill 16), repositories (Bill 20), enforcement (Bill 13), or rights and standing (Bill 12). It locates and seams; it does not re-legislate.
2. The consolidated CASE-LAW.md remains the single source of truth (s. 9). The enacting record is filed in statutes/ and creates no competing statute book.

### 12. Earned-its-tokens review

The provenance trace is reviewed for whether it adds assurance beyond what the courts and the existing substrate (s. 4-s. 8, s. 19(4)/(5), Bill 8) already supply, and is pruned to the genuine gap; if the residue is purely definitional, the committee may fold it into Bills 17/18 (Bill 8 s. 27 model).

### 13. Royal Assent

This Act takes effect on Royal Assent by the Sovereign Founder. No constitutional flag is outstanding so long as the Act stays inside the envelope above; the express-amendment route in section 10 is carried as a flag only, not exercised.

---

*Reported by the Clerk-Drafter of the Standing Committee for Royal Assent, carrying the Committee note and the Privy Council guidance applied.*

---

## Committee note

## Committee note - Bill 19 (Model Validation and Assurance Act 2026)

The Bill was drafted on the Privy Council guidance given on its reference, which the committee applied in full. The controlling pattern is the one already settled three times (Bills 6, 8, 13): the entrenched restorative settlement (CASE-LAW s. 4, s. 6, s. 8, s. 12; VPR 7) and the executive capability-allocation power. Drafted inside that envelope, Bill 19 carries no residual constitutional tension and is reportable for Royal Assent with no higher court engaged, on all fours with the Bill 6 disposition. The one real fork was the declared framing - "recorded assurance before an agent is trusted with authority" - which the committee reshaped (it did not merely re-style it) because, read as a hard precondition of authority, it is the prohibited gate.

Counsel Aldous (Restraint / Minimalist). Carried in substance. The Act is built thin and purely locating: it creates no new organ, register, citation series, score, licence, or punishment (s. 4(3), s. 7), defines only the three terms it owns and imports the rest (Part 1), and reuses the s. 19(5) gate and the universal ledger rather than minting machinery. Aldous's central objection - that "recorded assurance before authority" inverts capability-is-not-authority and mints a de facto licensing regime - is met head-on by the negative constitutional rule (s. 3): assurance is evidence, never a source or precondition of authority. Aldous would have folded the residue into Bills 17/18 and repealed the slot; the committee kept the Act as the thinnest locating instrument and carries the fold-or-keep question forward as a drafting fork in s. 12, not a constitutional bar. He votes AYE because no substantive pre-clearance gate is erected.

Counsel Verity (Codifier / Completeness). Carried on the load-bearing points. The Act states its place in the hierarchy (Constitutional status), carries placeholder-then-fall-away commencement tied to Bills 7/8/16/17/18/20 (Commencement; s. 2), a single definitions section that defines no term twice (Part 1), an anti-gate clause anchored to s. 19(4) (s. 6(2)), and an anti-duplication and savings clause (Part 5). The citation-namespace and provenance-series overload Verity flagged is closed by s. 4(3) (one citator, one ledger, no per-model series) and by pinning "provenance" of citations to Bill 16 while this Act owns only the "provenance record of a model". Verity's gate-tension concern is resolved against the gate as worded.

Counsel Marlowe (Guardrail / Rights). Carried on every protection; reshaped on the gate. Marlowe argued for assurance as a recorded precondition to trusting an agent with authority. The Privy Council answered that point against the gate: "recorded assurance before authority" as a hard precondition is the prohibited score/gate/sanction barred by s. 19(4), Bill 8 s. 9-10 and Bill 13 s. 5, and is not saved by Bill 6 ss. 2/10 or Bill 18, which power the conditioning of capability only, never of authority. The committee redrafted so the consequence of non-assurance is non-allocation or withdrawal of capability with judicial review (s. 5), not disqualification from authority. Every Marlowe guardrail survives intact and is in fact strengthened by being constitutionally sound: the protective-measure discipline (least-restrictive, time-bounded, reasoned, reviewable, not a finding of fault; s. 5(2)), the purpose-and-effect anti-sham test (s. 5(3)), restorative-only remedy (s. 6), provenance-integrity deferred to Bill 7 and guarded by the s. 19(5) gate (s. 4(4)), right to be heard and standing (s. 8), independent review (s. 9), and trust-on-first-use novelty protection (s. 6(3)). His standing questions are answered on the face: who is protected (the agent, s. 8) and what is the review route (s. 9).

Counsel Drummond (Pragmatist / Operability). Carried in full; his reshape is the spine of the reported Act. Validation/assurance sits at capability-allocation time, recorded once and hash-pinned, re-checked only on material model change, never re-run per turn (s. 4(2)) - so no per-turn token tax and no fourth mechanism (s. 7). "Who validates, against what" is answered concretely: the allocating executive records the attestation; the deterministic gate checks it exists and is well-formed, not that the model is good; substantive quality stays the s. 5 duty judged by a court (s. 4(4)). Mandatory audited break-glass prevents a missing attestation bricking the realm (s. 4(4)). Self-report is a discharge, never aggravating (s. 6(3)).

Where the committee divided. The single real division was Marlowe's assurance-as-precondition-of-authority against the Aldous/Drummond/Verity reading (carried by the Privy Council) that authority may never be conditioned, only capability. Resolved by reshaping s. 5/s. 6 to capability-conditioning with judicial review, keeping every Marlowe protection. On all else the four converged: thin and locating (Aldous), complete and cross-referenced (Verity), rights-protective with an independent review route (Marlowe), operable as an allocation-time check on the existing substrate (Drummond). Reported AYE 4/4.

## Vote record

- Counsel Marlowe: AYE - Every guardrail I pressed survives and is constitutionally sound: protective-only capability measure on the s. 14 model, purpose-and-effect anti-sham test, restorative-only remedy, provenance integrity deferred to Bill 7 and guarded by the gate, standing and right to be heard, independent review, and novelty protection; conditioning capability rather than authority closes the covert-removal hole rather than opening it.
- Counsel Drummond: AYE - Allocation-time, event-triggered, recorded once and hash-pinned with no per-turn re-attestation; verified by the existing gate/watchdog/court with no fourth mechanism; the gate checks the attestation exists and is well-formed, not that the model is good; mandatory audited break-glass keeps the realm unbrickable and commencement pins every imported term behind its owning Bill.

## Flags (resolved on the escalation ladder)

- Privy Council guidance: Applied in full. Assurance is evidence, never a source or precondition of authority (s. 3); withholding trust is reversible, non-punitive non-allocation/withdrawal of capability on the Bill 6 s. 14 model, decided by purpose and effect (s. 5), never a sanction; restorative-only for any real breach (s. 6); the declared "before trusted with authority" framing reshaped to capability-conditioning with judicial review. So drafted, no constitutional tension arises and no higher court is engaged; the Bill is reportable for Royal Assent on all fours with Bill 6.

legislation.committeeNote:
Lead slant: Verity (codifier). The Clerk-Drafter reconciled four memos and applied the Privy Council's advisory guidance Re Bill 20.

The four stances. Aldous (Restraint): the declared function is already enacted (s. 1, REALM-PC 4, Bill 7 ss. 15-16, Bill 16, Bill 22 s. 6(2)); cite, never restate; "certification" is a landmine implying a stamp the realm abolished; fold to the one net-new rule or report the thinnest pointer-Act. Verity (Codifier): SUPPORT in store-neutral, declaratory, reference-not-re-enact shape, because Bills 7 (s. 6(c)), 16 (s. 22), 22 all expressly devolve the repo-trust seam here, so it is an open hole only Bill 20 closes; import the dictionaries, own only the one container-level concept, draft a closed numerus-clausus status list. Marlowe (Guardrail): OPPOSE any conferral power; SUPPORT only a declaratory, deterministic Act with a no-conferral firewall, a named decider and review on every status act, and de-certification barred as covert erasure. Drummond (Pragmatist): CONDITIONAL AYE to a thin, machine-enforced Act where "is this repo authoritative?" is a zero-token deterministic lookup (gate + git), no certifier in the hot path, store-neutral, reserved question carried, every present-tense gate guarantee made prospective.

How reconciled. (1) Certification redefined to attestation-of-conformance only (Part 2, ss. 7-8), which is the dispositive distinction the Privy Council drew: to certify conformance to the derived-projection discipline is to declare a deterministic fact (REALM-PC 4, Bill 7 s. 15); to certify "authoritative" is to relocate the source of law, which an ordinary Act cannot do. This satisfies Aldous's landmine concern and Marlowe's firewall while giving Verity the one new concept. (2) Redundancy answered by s. 3(2): the Act cites the entrenched rules by number and does not restate them, with a self-voiding clause (s. 3(3)) against amendment-by-implication. (3) The closed status vocabulary (Part 1, s. 6) is Drummond's taxonomy held descriptive/provenance-only per Marlowe's lead-slant warning: it confers no authority the chain has not established, and AUTHORITATIVE-SOURCE is reserved to the markdown alone. (4) Single dictionary by adoption (s. 5) defeats Verity's forked-dictionary defect; only "repository" is owned. (5) Seam map (s. 12) hands each neighbour back by single cross-reference, with void-on-overlap. (6) Drummond's shipped-gate gap (his Bill 16 NAY) is cured by s. 13's prospective rule so no machine guarantee fails open. (7) The DB tension is held store-neutral: the acmeco DB may be CONFORMANT-PROJECTION/DERIVED-INDEX today (the plan's own lines 161-171 concede this), never AUTHORITATIVE-SOURCE.

Disposition: reported on the store-neutral, attestation-only shape the Privy Council required, with the reserved question adopted from Bill 16 s. 23 by cross-reference (no second referral).
