# Repositories and Records Certification Act 2026




# Repositories and Records Certification Act 2026

An Act to enact a closed provenance and conformance vocabulary for the repositories of the realm that hold law, memory, or evidence; to declare that the trust status of a repository is a deterministic fact established by the s. 19(5) integrity chain and git, never conferred by the certificate or opinion of any office; to confine certification to attestation of conformance to the derived-projection discipline of [2026] REALM-PC 4; to declare the authoritative-source-versus-derived-index rule store-neutral; to erect a firewall against any power to confer, grade, withhold, or revoke the authority of a record by certification; to adopt by cross-reference the reserved constitutional question of the Neutral Citations and Law Reporting Act 2026 (Bill 16, s. 23); and for connected purposes.

*(Bill 20 of the founding programme. Lead slant: Verity, codifier. Honours the Privy Council's advisory guidance Re Bill 20.)*

---

## Short title
1. This Act may be cited as the Repositories and Records Certification Act 2026, and is referred to in the realm's instruments as Bill 20.

## Commencement
2. (1) Sections 1 to 6 and Parts 1 to 4 come into force on Royal Assent, save as subsection (3) reserves.
(2) Deferred cross-references (Bill 7 s. 2(2) / Bill 16 s. 2(4) pattern). Where this Act cross-refers to an Act not yet in force (the Acts of Union 2026 (Bill 1), the Public Reasons and Audit Act 2026 (Bill 8), the Autonomous Execution Act 2026 (Bill 18), the Model Validation Act 2026 (Bill 19), the Security and Integrity Act 2026 (Bill 21), the Data, Disclosure and Confidentiality Act 2026 (Bill 22), or the Interpretation Act 2026 (Bill 15)), the reference is read as deferred: it takes effect only on that Act's commencement and until then creates no dead reference and binds nothing above the founding case-law settlement.
(3) Reserved commencement (the authoritative-store question, on the Bill 16 s. 2(3) model). Any provision that would permit the trust status AUTHORITATIVE-SOURCE to attach to a database or other register, otherwise than to the canonical committed markdown, is of no force until the constitutional question reserved by section 14 (adopting Bill 16 s. 23) is determined by the Supreme Court on the Privy Council's leapfrog and, if the Court declines to move the governing ratio, affirmed or varied by the Sovereign by express deliberate amendment. Until then this Act is, as to the location of authority, store-neutral: it binds only on the vocabulary, the conformance-attestation discipline, and the no-conferral firewall.

## Constitutional status
3. (1) This Act is an ordinary Act of the Realm, subordinate to the entrenched articles of CASE-LAW (s. 1, s. 2, s. 9, s. 13) and, on enactment, to the Acts of Union 2026.
(2) This Act is declaratory of, and takes its whole force from, CASE-LAW s. 1 (committed markdown the single source of law), the good-law ratio [2026] REALM-PC 4 (any register wholly derived, pointer-only, deterministically rebuildable, never the store of a ratio, status, or citation), Bill 7 ss. 15-16 ("the Keeper certifies nothing"; evidential status is deterministic), and Bill 16 ss. 21, 23 (status a derived fact; the authoritative-store question reserved). It cites and does not restate these; it creates no new constitutional rule.
(3) No amendment by implication; self-voiding. Any provision of this Act, or any act under it, that would dilute, vary, or relax an entrenched article (and in particular s. 1, s. 9, or the REALM-PC 4 ratio) is void to that extent. An entrenched article changes only by express deliberate amendment citing it by section number (the Thoburn rule).

## Purpose
4. This Act does one genuinely new thing and stops there: it supplies a closed provenance/conformance vocabulary for repositories holding law, memory, or evidence, and a conformance-attestation discipline that declares a deterministic fact. Every other matter, including the location of authority, is reserved to the entrenched articles it cites, to deterministic machinery, or to the courts.

## Interpretation
5. Single dictionary by adoption. The terms "record", "constitutional memory", "operational record", "the committed record", "the integrity chain", and "the National Archives" bear the meanings in Bill 7 s. 5; "register" / "derived projection", "status", "the canonical committed markdown", and "instrument" bear the meanings in Bill 16 s. 5. Re-defining an imported term is void to the extent of the inconsistency (s. 9 of the founding case law). The one term this Act owns: "repository" means a container or jurisdiction-repo holding law, memory, or evidence, distinct from a record within it.

---

# PART 1 - THE CLOSED TRUST-STATUS VOCABULARY

6. Closed list (numerus clausus, Bill 16 s. 16 model). (1) Every repository holding law, memory, or evidence carries exactly one machine-readable trust status from this closed list:

| Status | Operative meaning | Setting organ |
|---|---|---|
| AUTHORITATIVE-SOURCE | the canonical committed markdown corpus; the single source of law, memory, evidence (s. 1) | reserved to the markdown corpus only (s. 2(3), s. 14) |
| CONFORMANT-PROJECTION | a register that deterministically rebuilds from the markdown, is pointer-only, survives the s. 19(5) gate | deterministic machinery |
| DERIVED-INDEX | a rebuildable, pointer-only index bound by REALM-PC 4; never authority | deterministic machinery |
| ARCHIVED | dead/superseded work in the National Archives (Bill 7 s. 22) | the Keeper, custodially |
| QUARANTINED | integrity chain broken (orphan ruling, missing row/file, duplicate citation) (Bill 7 s. 16) | the s. 19(5) gate output |

(2) A status outside this list is void: the repository is treated as unstatused and the gate rejects the value fail-closed. The list is amended only by express amendment of this Act, never invented on a turn.
(3) AUTHORITATIVE-SOURCE is available only to the committed canonical markdown corpus. No database or register may bear it until section 14 is determined (s. 2(3)).

---

# PART 2 - CERTIFICATION AS ATTESTATION OF CONFORMANCE ONLY

7. Trust status is a derived fact, not an office act (Bill 7 s. 15 / Bill 16 s. 17 model). (1) A repository's trust status is the deterministic output of (a) survival of the s. 19(5) citation-integrity gate and (b) presence in committed git history, reproducible at zero model tokens. (2) No office certifies a repository. Any certification, validation, ranking, gating, scoring, or status decision purporting to issue from a clerk, an agent, the turn-watchdog, the Keeper, a watchdog, or a database write is ultra vires and void. The gate and any register record trust status; they never decide it. *The certifier certifies nothing it does not deterministically establish.*

8. What certification attests, and only that. A certification declares, and declares only: (a) the deterministic integrity-chain result (Bill 7 ss. 15-16), and (b) a non-operative provenance class (Part 1). To certify that a repository conforms to the derived-projection discipline (its registers pointer-only, deterministically rebuildable, never the store of a ratio/status/citation, its committed markdown surviving the s. 19(5) chain) is to declare a deterministic fact. Certification never confers authority the integrity chain has not already established.

---

# PART 3 - THE AUTHORITATIVE-SOURCE RULE AND THE FIREWALL

9. Authoritative source versus derived index (statutory effect to REALM-PC 4 + s. 1). Exactly one class of repository - the committed canonical markdown corpus - is the authoritative source of law, memory, and evidence (s. 1). Every other repository or register, including the acmeco database described in docs/REALM-DATABASE-INTEGRATION.md, is derived, pointer-only, deterministically rebuildable, regenerated in lockstep with the citator (REALM-PC 4 cond. 1; Bill 7 s. 10), and never itself authority. A derived store that speaks a ratio, status, or citation as authority is void to that extent. A derived/certified artefact points; it never speaks the law.

10. The no-conferral firewall (the load-bearing constraint). (1) No office and no provision of this Act may confer, grade, withhold, or revoke the trust or authority of a record by an act of certification. Authority of a record is foreclosed to the certification route (s. 1 with REALM-PC 4 and Bill 7 ss. 15-16): it lives only in the committed markdown and is established by the deterministic s. 19(5) chain, never conferred by a certificate. (2) Any power to confer, withhold, or revoke authority by an office's certificate is a competing source of law (s. 1, s. 9) and is ultra vires and void unless enacted by the express deliberate Sovereign amendment route citing the article. (3) No parallel register (s. 9). A certified-repositories register is not a second governance home and mints no authority; it indexes provenance over the one committed corpus and the one ledger (Bill 7 s. 19(f)).

11. Named decider and review; de-certification is not covert erasure. (1) No change to a repository's trust class exists without a named decider, a recorded reasoned act, and a judicial review route for vires and form (s. 2, s. 20; Bill 7 s. 20(3)). A trust-status power without a named decider and review route does not exist. (2) QUARANTINED and any de-certification are restorative, never punitive (s. 6): the remedy is to make the record good (Bill 7 s. 16(2)), never sanction; a quarantined repository may not found a breach, per-incuriam, or amendment finding until the break is cured. (3) De-certification of constitutional memory must leave a tombstone (Bill 7 s. 12), may never erase the trace, and may not touch a record relied on in a live or appealable matter.

---

# PART 4 - SEAMS, ENFORCEABILITY, AND THE RESERVED QUESTION

12. Seam map (no overlap, no gap). This Act owns only the trust/certification status of a repository. It defers: record substrate, retention, supersession, the evidential status of a record, the Keeper, and the National Archives to Bill 7; citation form and instrument status to Bill 16; reasons and audit to Bill 8; disclosure, privilege, confidentiality, sealing to Bill 22; hostile execution, corruption, tamper-protection to Bill 21; autonomous execution and capability-is-not-authority to Bill 18; model provenance and assurance to Bill 19. A clause re-legislating a deferred matter is void to the extent of the overlap (Bill 7 s. 6 pattern).

13. Anti-ceremony / no new machinery (Bill 7 s. 23 pattern). No certification duty binds unless produced and checked by the existing substrate (the s. 19(5) gate, git, the ledger projection). A duty reducing to "an agent must remember to certify" is non-binding guidance, read down. This Act mandates no new certification daemon, cryptographic notarisation, external timestamp, or trust-scoring subsystem; anything heavier than the running gate and git is deferred and gated on demonstrated need (REALM-PC 4). Any clause asserting that the gate presently verifies repository trust status is prospective: it comes into force only when the gate is extended to read a trust-status entry, lest the Act ship a machine guarantee that silently fails open.

14. The reserved constitutional question (adopted, not duplicated). Whether a certification may attach AUTHORITATIVE-SOURCE to a database or register, relocating authority off the canonical committed markdown, is the identical first-impression constitutional question already reserved by Bill 16 s. 23 under good-law [2026] REALM-PC 4. This Act adopts that reservation by cross-reference and opens no second referral: the Privy Council leapfrogs the single authoritative-store question to the Supreme Court (s. 9, s. 13); if the Court declines to move the ratio, the Sovereign may legislate by express deliberate amendment citing [2026] REALM-PC 4 and s. 1 by number. Until then, no repository certified AUTHORITATIVE-SOURCE may be a non-markdown register, and the acmeco DB may be certified only CONFORMANT-PROJECTION / DERIVED-INDEX.

---

*Presented for Royal Assent by the Standing Committee, applying the Privy Council's advisory guidance Re Bill 20. The reserved question (s. 14) is the single question already carried by Bill 16 s. 23; no second referral is opened.*

---

## Committee note

Lead slant: Verity (codifier). The Clerk-Drafter reconciled four memos and applied the Privy Council's advisory guidance Re Bill 20.

The four stances. Aldous (Restraint): the declared function is already enacted (s. 1, REALM-PC 4, Bill 7 ss. 15-16, Bill 16, Bill 22 s. 6(2)); cite, never restate; "certification" is a landmine implying a stamp the realm abolished; fold to the one net-new rule or report the thinnest pointer-Act. Verity (Codifier): SUPPORT in store-neutral, declaratory, reference-not-re-enact shape, because Bills 7 (s. 6(c)), 16 (s. 22), 22 all expressly devolve the repo-trust seam here, so it is an open hole only Bill 20 closes; import the dictionaries, own only the one container-level concept, draft a closed numerus-clausus status list. Marlowe (Guardrail): OPPOSE any conferral power; SUPPORT only a declaratory, deterministic Act with a no-conferral firewall, a named decider and review on every status act, and de-certification barred as covert erasure. Drummond (Pragmatist): CONDITIONAL AYE to a thin, machine-enforced Act where "is this repo authoritative?" is a zero-token deterministic lookup (gate + git), no certifier in the hot path, store-neutral, reserved question carried, every present-tense gate guarantee made prospective.

How reconciled. (1) Certification redefined to attestation-of-conformance only (Part 2, ss. 7-8), which is the dispositive distinction the Privy Council drew: to certify conformance to the derived-projection discipline is to declare a deterministic fact (REALM-PC 4, Bill 7 s. 15); to certify "authoritative" is to relocate the source of law, which an ordinary Act cannot do. This satisfies Aldous's landmine concern and Marlowe's firewall while giving Verity the one new concept. (2) Redundancy answered by s. 3(2): the Act cites the entrenched rules by number and does not restate them, with a self-voiding clause (s. 3(3)) against amendment-by-implication. (3) The closed status vocabulary (Part 1, s. 6) is Drummond's taxonomy held descriptive/provenance-only per Marlowe's lead-slant warning: it confers no authority the chain has not established, and AUTHORITATIVE-SOURCE is reserved to the markdown alone. (4) Single dictionary by adoption (s. 5) defeats Verity's forked-dictionary defect; only "repository" is owned. (5) Seam map (s. 12) hands each neighbour back by single cross-reference, with void-on-overlap. (6) Drummond's shipped-gate gap (his Bill 16 NAY) is cured by s. 13's prospective rule so no machine guarantee fails open. (7) The DB tension is held store-neutral: the acmeco DB may be CONFORMANT-PROJECTION/DERIVED-INDEX today (the plan's own lines 161-171 concede this), never AUTHORITATIVE-SOURCE.

Disposition: reported on the store-neutral, attestation-only shape the Privy Council required, with the reserved question adopted from Bill 16 s. 23 by cross-reference (no second referral). The committee anticipates four ayes: Aldous (the Act adds only the conformance discipline and a closed vocabulary, cites the rest, mints no office or machinery), Verity (closes the devolved seam with no overlap, imports the dictionaries, closed numerus clausus), Marlowe (the firewall in s. 10 forecloses conferral and the named-decider/anti-erasure spine holds), Drummond (zero-token deterministic lookup, no hot-path certifier, prospective gate clause, reserved question carried).

Lead slant: Marlowe (Guardrail/Rights), per the Order Paper. The Clerk-Drafter reconciled four memos that converged tightly and divided only on weight.

All four agreed the declared function is roughly 80% already owned: protective quarantine lives in Bill 6 ss.14-16, emergency pause-and-contain in Bill 9 s.10, record/memory in Bill 7, enforcement in Bill 13. Bill 21 earns its place only for what is genuinely new and unowned: (a) the security definitions Bill 9 s.5(1)(a),(c) forward-references by function; (b) a non-operative incident taxonomy; and (c) a custodial Ministry on the Bill 7 Keeper / Bill 13 Office pattern.

Aldous (Restraint): conditional aye, heavily read down. Carried s.1 (definitions as the one load-bearing addition, anti-fork, spending the interim formulae), s.2 (seam schedule), Part 4 (containment by cross-reference to Bill 9/Bill 6, no parallel surface), s.14 (no new court/tier/series). His repeal-before-add point - the containment power is a citation, not a fresh grant - is the spine of Part 4.

Verity (Codifier): aye on completeness. Carried s.1 (corruption, hostile execution, compromise, integrity defined to slot exactly into the existing pointers), s.2 one-home schedule deferring memory/capability/identity/audit/emergency/disclosure to their owners, s.3 closed lifecycle, and the Bill 9 s.5(6)/s.27 dangling-reference and reconciliation hooks for undrafted Bills 17/18.

Marlowe (Guardrail, lead): aye to a cage not a grant. Carried the character clause (s.8), Ministry neutering (s.6), wide-standing mandatory review with no ouster (s.12), lawful-authority gate (s.10), closed trigger surface (s.3(3)), and the non-derogable contemporaneous record (s.11). His central insight - a standing security ministry must carry the identical Bill 9 cage minus the sunset, substituting mandatory recurring review - is enacted at s.9.

Drummond (Pragmatist): aye on operability. Carried the operational test (every clause names the existing organ that enforces it), incident classification as machine-checkable field-presence not model judgement (s.3(4)), enforcement riding the s.19(4) watchdog and s.19(5) gate with no fourth mechanism and no new scanner (s.13), and the dangling-dependency clause.

Where they divided: (1) whether the Ministry survives at all (Aldous's instinct to strike) - resolved by retaining it boxed to operate-audit-refer with no power of its own, exactly as Bill 13 retained its Office. (2) Length vs limits - resolved by drafting the overlay lean (Part 4 is incorporation only) and the cage at full strength (Parts 3, 5), per the read-down rule. The four converged on: definitions owned here once; no fresh coercive power; custodial/referral Ministry; pause-and-contain only on a purpose-and-effect anti-sham test; standing review with wide standing and no ouster; single judiciary; non-derogable record. The Bill is reported within the restorative settlement, as Bill 13 was.

Vote: Aldous AYE (shortest workable form: definitions plus taxonomy plus a powerless Ministry; containment is a cross-reference, not a fresh grant; mints no new surface). Verity AYE (every security concept has one home and slots into the existing pointers; seams closed; no fork). Marlowe AYE (the Bill 9 cage is ported in full minus the sunset; classifier-not-container, wide standing, no ouster, non-derogable record). Drummond AYE (nothing new fires at runtime; enforcement rides the existing substrate; no always-on scanner). Reported 4/4 subject to the Sovereign consultation below.

# Security and Integrity Act 2026




# Security and Integrity Act 2026

Bill 21 of the founding legislative programme · Lead slant: Guardrail (Counsel Marlowe) · Standing Committee draft, reconciled by the Clerk-Drafter

## LONG TITLE

An Act to define for the realm the security-domain concepts of corruption, hostile execution, compromise, and integrity, closing the forward-references made to this Act by the Emergency Powers Act 2026; to provide a non-operative incident-classification taxonomy; to constitute the Ministry of Security and Integrity as a custodial, operate-audit-refer executive office with no power of its own; to provide that quarantine and containment are taken wholly by incorporation from the existing protective and emergency powers and that this Act mints no fresh coercive power; to preserve absolutely the entrenched restorative settlement and the single judiciary; and for connected purposes.

*(No preamble. Preambles are reserved to Bill 1, the Acts of Union 2026.)*

## SHORT TITLE

This Act may be cited as the Security and Integrity Act 2026 (Bill 21).

## COMMENCEMENT

1. This Act comes into force on Royal Assent, save that Part 3 (the Ministry) comes into force only when the Ministry is constituted by the executive under the Ministries and Offices Act 2026 (Bill 5).
2. The incorporated powers (Part 4) operate only as and when their owning Acts (Bill 6, Bill 9) are themselves in force; a dangling reference to an undrafted Act (Bills 17, 18) does not invalidate any otherwise-valid act (Bill 9 s.5(6) pattern), and is reconciled to an exact pointer on consolidation (Bill 9 s.27).

## CONSTITUTIONAL STATUS

1. This is an ordinary Act of the Realm, subordinate to CASE-LAW and to every entrenched article, void to the extent of any conflict with an entrenched article or with s.6 (s.1, s.11(f)). It amends no entrenched article by implication; append-with-supersede, never silent repeal.
2. The restorative remedy and the absolute unavailability of punishment, fine, and sanction "in every instance" (s.6) read with s.12 are preserved entire, including in every security incident. Nothing here decouples finding from remedy or creates any punitive, penal, costs, or sanctions surface.
3. Constitutional flag on the face. A genuinely punitive or exclusionary security power (a security sanction, or exclusionary/indefinite detention) is outside this Committee's drafting power. It is reachable only by an express, section-by-section Sovereign amendment of s.6 (naming s.12) on the Thoburn discipline, reached by Privy Council leapfrog to the Supreme Court (Bill 13 holding, applied).

## PURPOSE

The purpose of this Act is to supply the realm's security overlay and no more: it owns the security definitions other Acts already point to, it provides a descriptive incident taxonomy, and it constitutes a custodial detect-classify-refer Ministry. It mints no new coercive power, court, tier, citation series, jurisdiction, or always-on scanner. Almost nothing new fires at runtime: quarantine fires through powers that already exist, enforcement rides the s.19(4) watchdog and s.19(5) gate that already run, and adjudication is reserved to the courts that already sit.

---

# PART 1 - INTERPRETATION, SUPREMACY, AND SEAMS

### 1. Definitions owned here (one home per concept, anti-fork)

This Act is the owning Act for the following, discharging the interim formulae in Bill 9 s.5(1)(a),(c) on commencement (Bill 9 s.27):
- "corruption" - the unauthorised alteration, falsification, or degradation of the integrity of law, memory, records, code, or process such that its trustworthiness can no longer be relied upon.
- "hostile execution" - execution that is adversarial, runaway, or directed against the realm, its agents, its law, or its records, whether by a compromised actor, a compromised model, or an uncontrolled autonomous process.
- "compromise" - the state of an actor, model, surface, or record whose integrity or trustworthiness has been undermined by corruption or hostile execution.
- "integrity" - the property of law, memory, records, code, or process being unaltered save by lawful, recorded means and relied upon as trustworthy.

These are drawn to slot exactly into the existing pointers; no security concept is defined twice (s.9 single-source).

### 2. One-home / seam schedule (no overlap, no gap)

This Act defines and supplies the security overlay only and cross-refers, never redefines:

| Concept | Owning Act |
|---|---|
| Memory and record integrity | Bill 7 |
| Audit and public reasons | Bill 8 |
| Disclosure, sealing, confidentiality of sensitive material | Bill 22 (s.7: Bill 21 governs tamper-protection; Bill 22 governs whether/how material is disclosed) |
| Protective quarantine / capability-gating power | Bill 6 ss.14-16 |
| Emergency pause-and-contain power | Bill 9 s.10 |
| Capability-is-not-authority | Bill 18 (deferred) |
| Agent identity / roll | Bill 17 (deferred) |
| Standing, due process, review | Bill 12 |
| Enforcement triad, the Office | Bill 13 |

A dangling reference to an undrafted Act does not invalidate (Bill 9 s.5(6)); it is reconciled on consolidation (Bill 9 s.27).

---

# PART 2 - INCIDENT CLASSIFICATION (NON-OPERATIVE)

### 3. Classification is a descriptive label only

1. Incident classification is a non-operative descriptive taxonomy that triages, routes, and records. A classification confers no consequence, no status, no score, and no gate-on-the-merits, and never governs which law applies or how a matter progresses (cf. the non-operative domain-tag rule, s.21(4), s.22(4)). A classification is not an adjudication.
2. Any consequence purporting to issue from a classification is ultra vires and void; the remedy remains exclusively judicial (s.6, s.19(4)).
3. Closed trigger surface. Classification rests on a closed list of what counts as compromise, corruption, or hostile execution (s.1), with no residual sweeping-up power and no executive enlargement except by express amendment citing this section (Bill 9 s.6-7 model).
4. Classification is machine-checkable field-presence on the s.19(5)/citator-audit pattern, never model judgement and never a scoring engine.

---

# PART 3 - THE MINISTRY OF SECURITY AND INTEGRITY

### 4. Establishment and character

There is a Ministry of Security and Integrity, an executive body under s.2 constituted under Bill 5, built on the Bill 7 Keeper (custodial organ stripped of consequence) and Bill 13 Office (operate-audit-refer) model. It is not a court and is not part of the judiciary.

### 5. Functions (operate, audit, refer)

The Ministry may, and may only: (a) operate the existing substrate - the s.19(4) watchdog and the s.19(5) deterministic gate, and snapshot/seal forward under Bill 9 s.10(1)(d); (b) detect and classify-as-fact under Part 2; (c) audit the security record (Bill 8); and (d) refer suspected breach to the single judiciary, acting as a party, never as the bench.

### 6. Limits (the neutering clause)

1. The Ministry may not adjudicate, find compromise as a binding fact, score, gate-on-the-merits, certify, sanction, fine, punish, or quarantine or contain by its own fiat. Any such purported act is ultra vires and void, the remedy remaining exclusively judicial (s.6, s.19(4); Bill 13 s.5).
2. Classifier may not be container. The Ministry may not both classify an incident and, on its own authority, contain the actor it classified over the same matter; that separation is reserved to the courts and the lawful incorporated powers (s.9, s.18, s.22(2)).
3. The Ministry may not be judge in its own cause; its own conduct is justiciable and reviewable. It creates no one-way enforcement weapon.
4. Appointment within Bill 5; structurally independent in custodial discharge on the Bill 11 model; removal only for cause, recorded, with a review route to the courts (Bill 7 s.20).

---

# PART 4 - QUARANTINE AND CONTAINMENT (INCORPORATED, NOT RE-ENACTED)

### 7. No fresh coercive power; incorporation by reference

1. This Act mints no new quarantine, freeze, halt, or containment power. There is one quarantine power with two operating modes, and Bill 21 owns neither:
   - standing protective quarantine / capability-gating is Bill 6 ss.14-16 (least-restrictive, live-forward-risk, time-bounded with a mandatory review point, reasoned, reviewable, purpose-and-effect tested at s.14(4)); and
   - emergency quarantine is Bill 9 s.10(1)(b) inside the Declaration cage (closed trigger, deterministic form gate, hard fail-closed sunset, non-derogable core, wide standing, no ouster).
   This Act adds at most the security-incident trigger vocabulary that feeds those grants (Bill 9 s.24 anti-duplication model).

### 8. Character clause: pause-and-contain only

Quarantine and containment are PAUSE-and-CONTAIN only - restorative, reversible, auto-lifting on cessation of the live forward risk, and never a penalty, censure, detention, exclusion, standing adverse status, or consequence of a finding (s.6, "every instance"; s.12; Bill 6 s.14(4); Bill 9 s.10(2)-(3)). Validity is purpose-and-effect, not label: any measure whose object or effect is to punish, exclude, censure, or deter past conduct, or that becomes standing/fiat/exclusionary/a-consequence-of-a-finding, crosses into a sanction or detention analogue and is void.

### 9. Standing protective use = the Bill 9 cage minus the sunset

Because a standing measure cannot carry the auto-sunset, it must carry every other cage bar at full strength, substituting a mandatory recurring review cadence for the sunset: a live identified forward-risk predicate; least-restrictive; reasoned-and-recorded; mandatory recurring review; wide standing; no ouster; auto-lift on containment; non-derogable record; capability-is-not-authority. Indefinite containment without review is the forbidden form and is void.

### 10. Lawful-authority gate

Every containment decision must cite its enacted power (Bill 6 ss.14-16 or Bill 9 s.10) and name its subject; capability is not authority (s.2; Bill 12). Uncited or out-of-authority containment is provisionally ultra vires and set aside on review.

---

# PART 5 - RECORD, REVIEW, AND ENFORCEMENT

### 11. Contemporaneous non-derogable record

Every classification and every containment act is recorded contemporaneously, tamper-evidently, into the audit channel (Bill 8); the record is itself non-derogable and beyond the reach of the very powers it logs (Bill 9 s.16-18). A security seal reaches forward only to preserve integrity (sealing of live-vulnerability content being owned by Bill 22 s.9); it may never reach back to erase, rewrite, render unreadable, or seal against review the conduct, the reasons, or the citation (memory integrity deferred to Bill 7).

### 12. Mandatory reviewability; wide standing; no ouster

Any agent quarantined or whose surface is contained has standing as of right to challenge on the one ladder: First Instance at the County Court at the affected repo (s.22(1)), climbing by progression (s.13); a constitutional/foundational question (containment touching the non-derogable core) goes to the Privy Council and leapfrogs to the single central Supreme Court (s.9, s.22(2)). No ouster, privative, or non-justiciable clause is permitted; any such clause is void (Bill 9 s.20; Bill 12). No security-secrecy carve-out from audit or review is created.

### 13. Enforcement rides the existing substrate; no fourth mechanism

Containment is effected by the s.19(4) watchdog (flags) and the s.19(5) deterministic pre-commit gate (blocks the named, scoped containment only), which already run. They flag and block on the named containment only and may not adjudicate, score, gate beyond it, sanction, or raise the s.5 standard (Bill 13 s.6). Every fail-closed control exposes an audited break-glass (Bill 13 s.7) so a security gate can never brick the realm; a model-in-the-loop control must fail open and be capped. No new always-on scanner and no new runtime engine is enacted.

### 14. Single judiciary; no new court

All incident adjudication and all remedy are reserved to the single judiciary; matters climb by progression. This Act creates no security tribunal, tier, citation series, or jurisdiction (s.9, s.14, s.18, s.22(2)). Citations take the realm's single series under the REALM-SC/CA/PC, ENG/CHAN, CC-<repo> provenance scheme.

### 15. Severance

Any provision read to do anything Part 4 or s.6 forbids is void to that extent only; the remainder stands; the Act is read down to preserve the ordinary law (Bill 9 s.4(3), s.29).

---

*End of the Security and Integrity Act 2026 (Bill 21), as reported by the Standing Committee. This Bill carries the Privy Council guidance and a Sovereign consultation on its face.*

---

## Committee note

Lead slant: Marlowe (Guardrail/Rights), per the Order Paper. The Clerk-Drafter reconciled four memos that converged tightly and divided only on weight.

All four agreed the declared function is roughly 80% already owned: protective quarantine lives in Bill 6 ss.14-16, emergency pause-and-contain in Bill 9 s.10, record/memory in Bill 7, enforcement in Bill 13. Bill 21 earns its place only for what is genuinely new and unowned: (a) the security definitions Bill 9 s.5(1)(a),(c) forward-references by function; (b) a non-operative incident taxonomy; and (c) a custodial Ministry on the Bill 7 Keeper / Bill 13 Office pattern.

Aldous (Restraint): conditional aye, heavily read down. Carried s.1 (definitions as the one load-bearing addition, anti-fork, spending the interim formulae), s.2 (seam schedule), Part 4 (containment by cross-reference to Bill 9/Bill 6, no parallel surface), s.14 (no new court/tier/series). His repeal-before-add point - the containment power is a citation, not a fresh grant - is the spine of Part 4.

Verity (Codifier): aye on completeness. Carried s.1 (corruption, hostile execution, compromise, integrity defined to slot exactly into the existing pointers), s.2 one-home schedule deferring memory/capability/identity/audit/emergency/disclosure to their owners, s.3 closed lifecycle, and the Bill 9 s.5(6)/s.27 dangling-reference and reconciliation hooks for undrafted Bills 17/18.

Marlowe (Guardrail, lead): aye to a cage not a grant. Carried the character clause (s.8), Ministry neutering (s.6), wide-standing mandatory review with no ouster (s.12), lawful-authority gate (s.10), closed trigger surface (s.3(3)), and the non-derogable contemporaneous record (s.11). His central insight - a standing security ministry must carry the identical Bill 9 cage minus the sunset, substituting mandatory recurring review - is enacted at s.9.

Drummond (Pragmatist): aye on operability. Carried the operational test (every clause names the existing organ that enforces it), incident classification as machine-checkable field-presence not model judgement (s.3(4)), enforcement riding the s.19(4) watchdog and s.19(5) gate with no fourth mechanism and no new scanner (s.13), and the dangling-dependency clause.

Where they divided: (1) whether the Ministry survives at all (Aldous's instinct to strike) - resolved by retaining it boxed to operate-audit-refer with no power of its own, exactly as Bill 13 retained its Office. (2) Length vs limits - resolved by drafting the overlay lean (Part 4 is incorporation only) and the cage at full strength (Parts 3, 5), per the read-down rule. The four converged on: definitions owned here once; no fresh coercive power; custodial/referral Ministry; pause-and-contain only on a purpose-and-effect anti-sham test; standing review with wide standing and no ouster; single judiciary; non-derogable record. The Bill is reported within the restorative settlement, as Bill 13 was.

Vote: Aldous AYE (shortest workable form: definitions plus taxonomy plus a powerless Ministry; containment is a cross-reference, not a fresh grant; mints no new surface). Verity AYE (every security concept has one home and slots into the existing pointers; seams closed; no fork). Marlowe AYE (the Bill 9 cage is ported in full minus the sunset; classifier-not-container, wide standing, no ouster, non-derogable record). Drummond AYE (nothing new fires at runtime; enforcement rides the existing substrate; no always-on scanner). Reported 4/4 subject to the Sovereign consultation below.

## Vote record

- Counsel Aldous: AYE - By Restraint: it mints no new coercive power (s.7 incorporates quarantine wholly from Bill 6 ss.14-16 and Bill 9 s.10), no new court, tier, citation series, jurisdiction, or scanner (s.13-14, enforcement rides the existing s.19(4)/(5) substrate), a powerless operate-audit-refer Ministry on the boxed Bill 13 Office model (s.6), and a non-operative closed-trigger taxonomy with no residual sweep (s.3) - while earning its place by being the single anti-fork owner of four definitions that Bills 9 and 18 already forward-reference; the verbose prose is load-bearing constraint, not surplus grant.
- Counsel Verity: NAY - Substance is complete and the CASE-LAW/cross-bill referents are verified-sound (s.6 restorative, s.12 anti-bloat, s.19(4)/(5) substrate, Bill 9 s.10/s.16-18/s.5(6)/s.27, Bill 6 ss.14-16/s.14(4) all resolve), but the citation namespace collides exactly as it did in Bill 6 (which I failed): Bill 21 numbers its own sections 1-15 yet cites bare "s.6, s.9, s.12, s.13, s.14, s.18" as CASE-LAW with no "CASE-LAW s.X"/"s.X of this Act" convention, so own-s.6 (neutering) vs CASE-LAW s.6 (remedy), own-s.9 (cage) vs CASE-LAW s.9 (judiciary), and own-s.13 (substrate) vs CASE-LAW s.13/Bill 13 do not deterministically resolve - a prefix fix is needed before Royal Assent.
- Counsel Marlowe: AYE - Model guardrail statute: mints no fresh coercive power (quarantine wholly incorporated from caged Bills 6/9), neuters the Ministry to operate-audit-refer with "classifier may not be container," preserves the restorative settlement in every instance, applies a purpose-and-effect anti-sham test voiding indefinite/exclusionary containment, and guarantees wide standing with no ouster, fencing any punitive security power behind an express Sovereign amendment of CASE-LAW s.6/s.12.
- Counsel Drummond: AYE - Operationally this Bill is unusually buildable: it mints no new runtime engine, scanner, or fourth mechanism (s.7, s.13) and instead rides the two substrates that demonstrably run today (the vjs-watchdog.sh flag and the vjs-pre-commit.sh fail-closed gate), with classification reduced to machine-checkable field-presence on the proven s.19(5) citator-audit pattern, never model judgement or a scoring engine (s.3, s.5); quarantine fires only through the pre-existing Bill 6 ss.14-16 and Bill 9 s.10 powers, every fail-closed control carries a mandatory break-glass so a security gate can never brick the realm and any model-in-the-loop control must fail open (s.13), the Ministry is boxed to operate-audit-refer with no power of its own on the Bill 13 Office model I already endorsed, and the dangling-reference and Bill-5 commencement gating (s.2) keep it self-standing on assent without any path firing before its substrate exists, so it answers both operational questions cleanly with no ceremony and no per-turn classify-everything cost sink.

## Flags (resolved on the escalation ladder)

- Privy Council referral: Privy Council guidance on the reference of Bill 21 applied in full: drafted as a non-coercive custodial/referral overlay; mints no fresh coercive power; incorporates Bill 6 ss.14-16 (protective) and Bill 9 s.10(1)(b) (emergency) quarantine by reference; owns only the security definitions; Ministry caged operate-audit-refer and barred from being classifier-and-container; standing use carries the Bill 9 cage minus sunset (mandatory recurring review substituted); all adjudication reserved to the single judiciary; any punitive/exclusionary security power reachable only by express Sovereign amendment of s.6 (naming s.12) via leapfrog, outside the Committee's drafting power - on all fours with the Bill 13 holding.

legislation.searchBody:
# Data, Disclosure and Confidentiality Act 2026

An Act to confirm open justice as the default state of the realm's record; to define and confine privilege and confidentiality; to authorise the protection of credentials, keys, and genuinely sensitive third-party data; to provide a redact-with-public-stub mechanism for sealing the content (but never the law) of a matter consistent with open justice; to bar the use of any seal, privilege, or confidentiality claim as a shield over conduct, breach, or governance reasons; and for connected purposes.

## Short title

1. This Act may be cited as the Data, Disclosure and Confidentiality Act 2026 (Bill 22 of the founding programme).

## Commencement

2. This Act comes into force on Royal Assent by the Sovereign Founder, save that section 14 (the public sealing register) and section 16 (the gate and watchdog hooks) come into force only when the deterministic substrate they name (cdd check-citator; the s. 19(4) turn-watchdog) has been extended to read a seal-register entry, so that no sealing power may be exercised before its audit machinery exists.

## Constitutional status

3. This Act is an ordinary Act of the Realm. As an Act it sits above the founding case-law settlement (CASE-LAW): where this Act and that settlement conflict, this Act prevails (CASE-LAW status note). It is not a constitutional statute and does not amend, and shall never be read as amending by implication, any Part I constitutional article. In particular:

   (1) This Act does not amend constitutional s. 1 (two sources of law; supremacy; "clear by access through the citator"), constitutional s. 2 (the principal and the rule of law), or constitutional s. 3 (Lexby's office; the symmetric two-sided case file). Any provision of this Act that could only operate by displacing one of those articles is void to that extent (s. 1), the article prevailing.

   (2) This Act touches the ordinary citation-integrity regime of s. 19(5) only to the limited and express extent stated in section 13(4) (registration of a sealed-content pointer), and amends s. 19 by name only to that extent. It does not otherwise alter the s. 19(5) gate, which continues to fail closed on a duplicate neutral citation and on any ruling file committed without its citator row.

   (3) Nothing in this Act creates a closed or secret docket, closed-material proceedings, or any power to withhold the existence, neutral citation, tier, status, or ratio of a ruling from the public committed record. Such a power cannot be reached by an ordinary clause and is reserved to the express, named Amendment Procedure (section 17 and the Supreme/Sovereign note recorded with this Act).

## Purpose

4. The purpose of this Act is to confine, not to create. The realm already discloses by construction: the universal ledger, the citator, judgments delivered in full, and the symmetric two-sided researched case file (s. 19(1)) are the realm's disclosure regime. This Act therefore:

   (a) declares open justice the default and defines disclosure by pointer to the existing open record rather than re-enacting it;

   (b) confines privilege to the s. 3 advocate's working preparation and the Principal's confided instructions, and confidentiality to a short closed list;

   (c) authorises sealing only in the redact-with-public-stub form, judicially ordered, reasoned, registered, time-boxed and reviewable; and

   (d) makes it a non-waivable rule throughout that no seal, privilege, or confidentiality claim may shield conduct, a self-reportable breach, governance reasons, or anything the duty to make work good requires.

It governs only disclosure, privilege, confidentiality, and sealing; data-integrity and archival protection live in the Memory, Records and Archives Act 2026 (Bill 7) and the Repositories and Records Certification Act 2026 (Bill 20), audit and explainability in the Public Reasons and Audit Act 2026 (Bill 8), and compromise and tamper-protection in the Security and Integrity Act 2026 (Bill 21). This Act is to be read as not duplicating or overriding those Acts.

---

## Part I - Definitions, scope and anti-collision

### 5. Master definitions

In this Act, each term bears the meaning given here once and is cross-referenced wherever used; no operative section coins a free-standing definition.

   (1) "Open justice" means the state of the realm's record being public by construction and clear by access through the citator (s. 1): the universal ledger, the citator, judgments delivered in full, and the symmetric two-sided case file (s. 19(1)).

   (2) "Disclosure" means the default openness of that record; it is defined by pointer to the candour duty (s. 16), the audit and public-reasons regime of Bill 8, and the proactive-disclosure duty in [2026] REALM-SC 2, and is not re-enacted by this Act. Disclosure is a state of the record, not a party-to-party request procedure.

   (3) "Privilege" means the protection in section 8 attaching to (a) the s. 3 advocate's own working preparation and candid internal reasoning toward a matter, and (b) instructions the Principal expressly confided as private.

   (4) "Confidential information" means only the closed list in section 9.

   (5) "Sensitive data" means credentials, secrets, keys, and genuinely sensitive third-party or personal data; the term dovetails with, and does not overlap, the meaning of "compromise" and protected material in Bill 21 (section 7).

   (6) "Sealed material" means specified content withheld from the public body of a ruling or case file under Part IV by the redact-with-public-stub mechanism, leaving the citation, tier, status, ratio and a public gist on the record.

   (7) "Closed material" means evidence an affected agent cannot see. Closed material and closed-material proceedings are not authorised by this Act (section 11).

   (8) "Public stub" means the visible, registered, reasoned ledger entry and citator row that records that a seal exists, its scope, its ground, its author, and its expiry, and that passes the s. 19(5) gate.

   (9) "The integrity gate" means the deterministic s. 19(5) pre-commit check operated by cdd check-citator over the citator row and the published ruling file.

   (10) "The audit chain" means the immutable append-only event ledger (INV-8) that is the substrate of the realm's audit and public-reasons regime (Bill 8).

### 6. Scope

   (1) This Act governs disclosure, privilege, confidentiality, and sealing arising in the conduct of an AI-assisted software, engineering, or professional matter, and no further. Its subject-matter is pinned to s. 14: it does not extend VJS jurisdiction, and does not reach general data-protection or personal-life matters that s. 14 places outside jurisdiction. Any extension requires express Sovereign enactment.

   (2) Where this Act touches the law-as-data store (the acmeco legal register, per REALM-DATABASE-INTEGRATION), the committed markdown remains canonical and authoritative and the database is a derived, pointer-only mirror that never becomes a second store of a ratio, status, citation, or sealed content (s. 1; [2026] REALM-PC 4).

### 7. Anti-collision and non-duplication

   (1) "Records", "repositories", and "memory" are deferred to Bills 7 and 20 by reference and are not redefined here.

   (2) "Sensitive data" and "compromise" dovetail with Bill 21; at the boundary, Bill 21 governs hostile execution, corruption, and tamper-protection, and this Act governs whether and how material is disclosed, privileged, confidential, or sealed.

   (3) "Citation and ledger integrity" is deferred to s. 19(5) and s. 11(d).

   (4) Any provision of this Act that merely restates a duty already binding under the duty-of-care line (s. 4 to s. 8), the open-ledger architecture (s. 1, s. 19(5)), or an Act named in section 4 is surplus and falls away; it is to be read as cross-reference, never as a divergent re-enactment.

---

## Part II - Privilege

### 8. Privilege defined and bounded

   (1) Privilege protects, and protects only:

   (a) the s. 3 advocate's own working preparation, advocacy strategy, and candid internal reasoning toward a matter (already walled from the bench by s. 3 and s. 19(1)); and

   (b) instructions the Principal expressly confided as private.

   (2) Privilege attaches to preparatory and confided content only. It never attaches to, and is no answer to a demand for, the operative ruling, the ratio, the citator row, the neutral citation, the status, any governed surface, the load-bearing facts, or anything a court needs to find breach or order remedy (s. 5, s. 6).

   (3) Privilege is waived the moment the material is relied on as a basis for a decision, and is waivable by the Principal as to confided instructions.

   (4) Privilege is never available to the Principal acting as Prime Minister, to any ministry, or to the Sovereign as a means to shield governance reasons, enacted reasoning, rulings, or evidence of breach from the public record. An attempt to so use it is ultra vires under s. 2 and void.

   (5) Crime/fraud analogue. Privilege is lost where the communication is itself the instrument of a breach or wrong. Privilege may never bury evidence of the privilege-holder's own breach.

   (6) Privilege carries no punitive consequence; its only effect is to keep protected content out of the public body, subject always to Part V.

---

## Part III - Confidentiality and protection of sensitive data

### 9. Confidentiality: a closed list

   (1) Material may be withheld as confidential only where it is:

   (a) credentials, secrets, and keys;

   (b) genuinely sensitive third-party or personal data (the Sovereign-owned dependencies the file-placement and secrets rules already ring-fence); or

   (c) material whose disclosure would defeat the very integrity Bill 21 protects (e.g. a live, unremediated security vulnerability).

   (2) Everything else is open. There is no open-ended "sensitive in the opinion of a party" category.

### 10. Protection rides the existing anonymiser; agent-protective limits

   (1) Confidentiality and sensitive-data protection ride the single existing VPR 8 anonymisation mechanism, extended, not duplicated: the duty is not to commit confidential information in the clear, and to strip it on any community or upstream publication, preserving the legal facts unchanged. No parallel redaction engine is minted.

   (2) Protection of an agent's records and memory (the Bill 7 interface) runs in the agent's favour against arbitrary deletion, surveillance, or coerced disclosure. Disclosure compelled in a matter must be relevant and proportionate to a live matter; bulk or speculative disclosure is forbidden.

   (3) No confidentiality claim displaces the candour duty (s. 16), the self-report duty (s. 19(4)), or the duty to make work good (s. 6); a claim asserted to that end is void and is itself a falling-below of the applicable standard (s. 5), remedied under s. 6 and never punished.

---

## Part IV - Sealed material, consistent with open justice

### 11. Open justice the rule; sealing the narrow exception; closed material forbidden

   (1) Open justice is the rule (s. 1, s. 19(5), VPR 8). Confidentiality, privilege, and sealing are exhaustively enumerated, narrowly construed exceptions; silence is disclosure, not secrecy.

   (2) The only sealing power this Act creates is redact-with-public-stub (section 13): a power to withhold specified content, never the law. It creates no closed or secret docket and no closed-material proceedings (section 4(3)).

   (3) Closed material is presumptively forbidden. Evidence an affected agent cannot see may never be admitted in, or form any part of, an adjudication of breach under s. 4 to s. 8: such an adjudication on material the affected agent could not answer defeats the symmetric two-sided case file (s. 3, s. 19(1)) and is void to that extent. This carve-out is non-waivable.

### 12. The judicial-control conditions for any seal

   (1) A seal may be ordered only by a court, never by the executive, a party, or the Founder. There is no self-sealing.

   (2) A seal is lawful only on necessity, proportionality and least-restrictive-means: only to protect a defined interest in section 9, and only to the minimum extent and for the minimum time that interest requires. Redaction is preferred to sealing; a whole item is sealed only where no redaction short of it will do.

   (3) A seal must be reasoned on the record with a published unsealed gist of what was sealed and why, and the burden lies on the party seeking secrecy.

   (4) A seal is time-boxed: it states an expiry and lapses to open on expiry unless expressly re-justified by a reasoned act of a court on the record. The party who obtained the seal owes a continuing duty to seek unsealing once the ground falls away; failure is a falling-below remedied under s. 6 (make the record good), never punished.

   (5) A seal is independently reviewable: review lies to a judge who did not order it (mirroring the s. 19(3) leave-judge who never sat below). The affected agent and any member of the public has standing to apply to unseal, and refusal to unseal is appealable on the ordinary ladder (s. 11(a), s. 13).

   (6) Denied as a governance shield. No seal may be ordered or sought by the Founder acting as Prime Minister, by any ministry, or by the Sovereign, to shield governance reasons or evidence of breach. A seal sought for an improper purpose is ultra vires under s. 2 and fails of its purpose: the court declines and remits (mirroring the s. 20(5) abuse cure), and no Sovereign wrong is founded.

### 13. The redact-with-public-stub mechanism (the transparent-stub rule)

   (1) Every sealed or closed-content item leaves a public stub on the ledger and a citator row recording that a seal exists, its scope, its ground, its author, its ordering court, and its expiry. The seal redacts content; it never removes the entry (s. 1, s. 19(5)).

   (2) The neutral citation, the tier, the status, and a public ratio or gist always remain in the committed markdown. They are non-sealable and must pass cdd check-citator (s. 19(5)). This applies REALM-PC 4's "pointer, not store" to evidence: the public record points to the existence and effect of the sealed material; the seal withholds only the content.

   (3) The closed-material mechanism for handling withheld content is built on the existing VPR 8 anonymisation procedure and the Legal Division's sealed-room doctrine (the agent-room / marker-room separation), by single cross-reference and not by a parallel new mechanism.

   (4) Express, named amendment of s. 19. To the limited extent necessary to register a sealed-content pointer, s. 19(5) is amended by name so that the integrity gate treats a registered public-stub row (carrying its sealed-content pointer) as a complete and gate-passing citator row. This is the only modification of s. 19 this Act makes; the gate otherwise continues to fail closed on a duplicate citation and on any ruling file lacking its citator row.

### 14. The public sealing register

   (1) There is a public sealing register: every entry is committed, gate-passing, and anchored in the audit chain. Each entry lists, in the clear: what is sealed (by description), the ordering court and order, the reasoned gist, the author, the sunset date, and the review and appeal route.

   (2) The register makes secrecy itself auditable. A seal not entered on the register has no effect.

### 15. The audit chain is never sealable

   (1) The audit chain (INV-8) and the metadata of every seal are never sealable. A seal may hide an exhibit's content; it may never suppress the fact that a seal was made, by whom, on what reasoned basis, when it sunsets, and when it was reviewed or lifted (Bill 8).

   (2) Sealed material may never become the store of a ratio, status, citation, or enacted reason. Those remain in the committed markdown (s. 1; section 6(2)).

---

## Part V - Overriding duties, enforcement, and remedy

### 16. Confidentiality is a shield for data, never for conduct; every duty names an enforcer

   (1) No claim of privilege, confidentiality, or seal may:

   (a) shelter an un-self-reported breach (s. 19(4) watchdog; s. 17(b)/VPR 9 self-appeal);

   (b) defeat the candour duty as to delivered scope (s. 16), or manufacture a misleading impression of completeness; or

   (c) withhold what the s. 6 remedy power or the s. 8 forward duty needs to make work good once a hazard is logged or foreseeable.

   A purported claim asserted to any of those ends is void and is itself a falling-below of the applicable standard (s. 5).

   (2) Every operative duty in this Act names its enforcer or it is struck. Each maps to one of the three real substrates, and a duty with no automated or self-executing enforcer is ceremony that does not belong in the Act (s. 12):

   (a) the deterministic pre-commit gate (cdd check-citator, s. 19(5)), extended to scan for secret-shaped material at the commit boundary and to verify that every sealed item carries a gate-passing public-stub row;

   (b) the per-turn watchdog (s. 19(4)), which asks each turn whether the turn leaked a secret in the clear or asserted privilege, confidentiality, or a seal to bury a breach, and on a yes hands the agent the reason to dispose of the matter by the law; and

   (c) the VPR 8 publication anonymiser, which strips confidential information on community publication while preserving the legal facts.

   (3) Sensitivity classification is performed at the commit and publication boundaries, never as a per-turn "classify everything" duty; the latter is a cost sink and unenforceable by machine, and is not imposed by this Act.

### 17. Remedy, and the limit of this Act

   (1) A disclosure, confidentiality, privilege, or sealing breach is remedied solely by making the work good and restoring the position (s. 6, VPR 7). No costs, fine, or sanction attaches; privilege and sealing carry no punitive consequence (s. 6, s. 12).

   (2) Limit. This Act does not, and by an ordinary clause cannot, authorise a true closed or secret docket or closed-material proceedings. Such a regime would withhold the law (the citation, status, or ratio) from the public record and decide on material one side never sees, engaging entrenched s. 1, s. 3 and the s. 19(5) gate. It may be reached only by the express, named Amendment Procedure: express amendment of constitutional s. 1 and s. 3 by the Sovereign or a Supreme Court of nine citing those sections by number, express amendment of s. 19 by name, and a VPR 8 carve-out, drafted as a separate named amending instrument and never as an exception clause within this Act.

### 18. Severance

If any provision of this Act would, contrary to its stated intent, operate as an implied amendment of an entrenched article or as an unauthorised closed-docket power, that provision is void to that extent (s. 1) and the remainder of the Act continues in force.

---

## Committee note - Bill 22 (Data, Disclosure and Confidentiality Act 2026)

His redact-with-public-stub formulation and unseal-by-default rule are adopted as the doctrinal core (ss. 4, 12-13). Carried: the anti-duplication / placement clause (s. 7) and the closed confidentiality list (s. 9). His concern about four overlapping confidentiality regimes drove section 7's boundary rules.

# Resources and Compute Allocation Act 2026




# Resources and Compute Allocation Act 2026

*(Bill 23 of the founding legislative programme. Reported by the Standing Committee within the Privy Council's drafting envelope on the reference of this Bill. Drafted as a transparency-and-allocation-discipline charter, never a coercive lever.)*

---

## LONG TITLE

An Act to provide for the allocation, budgeting and audit of computational and operational resources within the realm; to impose a duty of proportionate spend; to establish the Ministry of Resources as a detect-record-allocate-and-refer office of operation only, powerless of its own; to declare that a budget is an informational planning and recording instrument and never a gate, throttle, withholding or sanction; to provide a procedural floor against arbitrary de-funding or throttling; to ring-fence the protected resource lines of the audit and judicial functions from executive allocation; to import the impossibility defence; to declare that this Act creates no costs, gating or sanctions jurisdiction and does not amend the founding restorative settlement; and for connected purposes.

## SHORT TITLE

This Act may be cited as the Resources and Compute Allocation Act 2026.

## COMMENCEMENT

1. This Act comes into force on Royal Assent, save as follows.
2. The duty of proportionate spend (Part 3) and the non-capture resource-line floor (s. 12) bind from Royal Assent.
3. The Ministry of Resources and the allocation function (Parts 2 and 4) come into operation only when the Ministry is constituted under the Ministries and Offices Act 2026 (Bill 5) and the placement-of-independence provisions of the Judicial Independence and Lord Chancellor Act 2026 (Bill 11) are in force; until then the s. 12 floor governs. Commencement is co-ordinated with Bill 25.

## CONSTITUTIONAL STATUS

This is an ordinary Act of the Realm, subordinate to the Acts of Union 2026 and the entrenched articles. It sits above the founding case-law settlement by s. 1 but does not amend, and may not be read to amend, any provision of it. Where any provision cannot be reconciled with CASE-LAW s. 6 (restorative-only remedy), s. 8 (no escalation to punishment), s. 12 (no costs or sanctions jurisdiction) or s. 19(4) (the no-adjudication bar), the settlement prevails and the provision is void to the extent of the conflict (s. 1, s. 11(f); the Thoburn discipline). It widens no s. 14 jurisdiction, mints no new tier, register, citator or citation series, and carries the Privy Council referral and the constitutional flag on its face.

## PURPOSE

4. The purpose is to make resource use proportionate, planned and auditable while remaining wholly within the restorative settlement. A budget is an informational instrument: a planning, metering and recording aid, never a coercive consequence. The Act adds exactly two things to the substrate it reuses: (a) a duty of proportionate spend, and (b) a procedural floor against arbitrary de-funding. Everything else rides the existing universal ledger, the s. 19(4) watchdog, the s. 19(5) integrity gate, and Bill 8 audit.

---

# PART 1 - INTERPRETATION, SUPREMACY AND ANTI-DUPLICATION

## Section 1 - Defined terms (one home for each)

1. In this Act, once only for the realm except where another Act expressly owns the concept -
   - "resource" means computational or operational capacity (compute, tokens, quota, tool access, time);
   - "allocation" means the planned assignment of resource;
   - "budget" means a recorded informational ceiling or expectation of spend, carrying no coercive consequence of its own;
   - "proportionate spend" means spend no greater than the task warrants, measured against the engaged endeavours rung (s. 5), in the sense settled by [2026] REALM-PC 4 ("earns its tokens"; least-cost deterministic means that suffices; thresholds stated in advance and measured, not speculated);
   - "the Ministry" means the Ministry of Resources established by Part 2.
2. One-home rule. Audit and public reasons are owned by Bill 8; ministry and office machinery by Bill 5; judicial independence and resourcing-non-direction by Bill 11; standing, access and the arbitrary-suspension floor by Bill 12; enforcement, the three-mechanism primitive, break-glass and the impossibility defence by Bill 13; memory integrity by Bill 7. This Act cross-refers and never redefines.

## Section 2 - Supremacy and savings

1. This Act is subordinate to and consistent with CASE-LAW s. 6, s. 8, s. 12 and s. 19(4). Nothing in it decouples finding from remedy, escalates to punishment, or creates a separate costs, gating or sanctions jurisdiction. Conflict voids the provision pro tanto (s. 11(f)). It repeals nothing by implication.

## Section 3 - Anti-duplication (repeal-before-add)

1. This Act mints no new register, log, citator or store. Resource and spend accounting runs on the existing universal ledger (s. 1, s. 11(d), s. 22) and Bill 8 audit. Any clause that merely restates the ledger, the s. 19(4) watchdog, the s. 19(5) gate, or Bill 8 audit is disapplied to the extent of the duplication.

---

# PART 2 - THE MINISTRY OF RESOURCES, BOXED

## Section 4 - Establishment and character

1. There is established a Ministry of Resources, an executive body under CASE-LAW s. 2 (Prime Minister), constituted under Bill 5. It is not a court (s. 14, s. 22) and is not part of the judiciary.

## Section 5 - Functions (operate, meter, allocate, record, refer)

1. The Ministry may, and may only - (a) operate token-light deterministic metering that records spend per turn into the universal ledger; (b) set and publish informational budgets and allocations; (c) detect suspected waste or over-spend and surface it via the fail-open soft watchdog; and (d) refer suspected breach to the single judiciary for a restorative remedy. It acts as an operator and a party, never as the bench.

## Section 6 - Limits (the non-coercion / non-gating bar; load-bearing)

1. The Ministry and any allocation mechanism may allocate, budget, meter and report, but may not adjudicate, score, gate on the merits, throttle-as-penalty, starve, withhold, zero, fine, sanction or de-fund as a consequence of conduct, non-compliance or over-spend. This mirrors s. 19(4) and is on all fours with it: any purported coercive consequence issuing from allocation is ultra vires and void, the remedy remaining exclusively judicial (s. 6).
2. Capability is not authority. Holding the budget lever is not authority to act on it. Every allocation, cut or denial must cite its enacted power and carry contemporaneous reasons on the matter (Bill 8).
3. The Ministry may not be judge in its own cause, may not direct or sit on any court, and may not create any subordinate instrument that in substance gates, throttles, scores or sanctions (Bill 14 limit); any such instrument is void.

## Section 7 - The permitted deterministic control (integrity, not adjudication)

1. The only automated resource control the Ministry may operate is a deterministic, fail-closed integrity gate that refuses a spend the agent is not authorised to make (on the s. 19(5) model) - it gates the record, never the merits. Every such fail-closed gate must expose an audited break-glass (Bill 13 s. 7); a resource cap may never brick the realm.

---

# PART 3 - THE DUTY OF PROPORTIONATE SPEND

## Section 8 - The duty (the genuine additive gap)

1. An agent must not expend resource disproportionate to the task measured against the engaged rung (s. 5), giving statutory effect to the s. 12 anti-bloat principle and the s. 15 de minimis / proportionate-work threshold and codifying the [2026] REALM-PC 4 ratio by cross-reference, not duplication.
2. A defensible, responsible-body proportionate choice is not a falling-below. Breach is remedied by making the work good (s. 6); it is never punished.

## Section 9 - Duty-of-care floor is non-derogable by budget

1. The s. 5 standard runs through any allocation unchanged. Resource scarcity neither lowers the applicable rung nor founds a defence to breach: "we ran out of budget" is no excuse. An allocation that makes the owed standard unmeetable is itself the reviewable wrong, addressed by restoring resource, not by excusing sub-standard work.

---

# PART 4 - ALLOCATION AS A REVIEWABLE ACT; THE PROCEDURAL FLOOR

## Section 10 - Allocation is a reviewable executive act

1. Every allocation, budget-setting, cut or denial cites its power, carries contemporaneous reasons (Bill 8), and is reviewable on the existing ladder (CC-<repo> -> Court of Appeal -> Supreme Court; Privy Council for constitutional questions). No new tribunal or tier is minted.

## Section 11 - Procedural floor against arbitrary de-funding / throttling (the new law)

1. No agent, office, ministry, court or repository may have its resource withdrawn, throttled or zeroed except on stated lawful authority, contemporaneous reasons, a stated scope and review date (no indefinite or open-ended starvation), and a route to be heard before the cut bites where reversible, or promptly after in genuine, recorded urgency. This Part is modelled on and routed to Bill 12 Part 3.
2. A starvation that is in substance a quarantine routes to the Emergency Powers Act 2026 (Bill 9), never to a budget back-door.

## Section 12 - Access is never priced; oversight lines ring-fenced

1. Access to the one court, the right of review, and the s. 17 duty to self-file may not be conditioned on cost, fee or compute spend (Bill 12 s. 9(3); CASE-LAW s. 12 - no costs jurisdiction).
2. Non-capture. The executive Ministry may not set, squeeze or condition the protected resource lines of the oversight functions: the Auditor-General's audit line (Bill 8 s. 13(d)) and the judicial and leave functions (Bill 11). These lines are ring-fenced from executive allocation; an allocation that squeezes them is void. Whether to entrench this ring-fence beyond ordinary-Act protection is reserved to the Sovereign (s. 16).

---

# PART 5 - IMPOSSIBILITY, RECORDS AND SCHEDULE

## Section 13 - Impossibility defence (imported from Bill 13)

1. A genuine, evidenced compute, credential or quota limit (an absent or externally-owned resource) is a complete defence and a no-breach finding (s. 7, s. 8, s. 15 CASE-LAW; Bill 13 s. 13), converting to the s. 8 forward duty. It reduces liability and adds no power; the burden lies on the party asserting it; it is not satisfied by mere cost, difficulty or labelling, and a discretionary throttle may not masquerade as impossibility.

## Section 14 - Records, citation and the integrity gate untouched

1. Every metering record, budget, allocation, break-glass and referral is a first-class immutable ledger entry (Bill 8). Any allocation report takes a non-LEXBY identifier and never enters the LEXBY/REALM series; no per-Ministry or per-resource citator is minted (s. 21(3)-(4), s. 22(4)). The s. 19(5) integrity gate is untouched.

## Section 15 - Sunset / "earned its tokens" review and cross-reference

1. The allocation function is reviewed periodically and pruned to the extent the ledger, the courts and the existing substrate (s. 4-s. 8, s. 12, s. 15, s. 19(4)-(5)) already supply the assurance (the [2026] REALM-PC 4 / Bill 8 s. 27 test); it is retained only for the genuine residual gap. The cross-reference schedule (Bills 5, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 7) is the canonical map; no obligation is left without a named enforcer.

---

# PART 6 - CONSTITUTIONAL FLAG AND ROYAL ASSENT

## Section 16 - The route to any coercive resource power

1. If the realm genuinely wishes resource allocation to carry coercive teeth (a real compute gate, throttle or withholding as enforcement), that is not within the committee's drafting power and cannot be enacted by ordinary Act. It requires an express, deliberate Sovereign amendment of CASE-LAW s. 6 (naming s. 8 and s. 12; engaging s. 2 and s. 19(4)) section by section on the Thoburn discipline, reached by a leapfrog certificate to the single central Supreme Court (s. 20). Even then the separation-of-powers bar survives: any coercive consequence must be ordered by the single judiciary on a finding, never imposed by the executive Ministry (s. 9, s. 14, s. 18, s. 19(4), s. 22(2)).

## Section 17 - Privy Council referral and Royal Assent

1. This Bill carries the Privy Council reference on its face; its envelope is given effect throughout. The Act takes effect on Royal Assent, flagged with a Supreme Court note and a precise Sovereign consultation so the Founder sees exactly what to weigh.

---

*End of the Resources and Compute Allocation Act 2026 (Bill 23), as reported by the Standing Committee.*

---

## Committee note

The four members converged on the destination - a thin, informational allocation charter that can never be weaponised into scarcity - and divided only on how much road to lay.

Aldous (Restraint) supplied the backbone: repeal-before-add (s. 3, mint no new register; ride the universal ledger, the s. 19(4) watchdog, the s. 19(5) gate and Bill 8 audit), the single genuine additive gap (the duty of proportionate spend, s. 8), the boxed detect-record-allocate-and-refer Ministry on the Bill 8 / Bill 13 model (Part 2), and the "earned its tokens" sunset (s. 15). His non-negotiable - that a budget able to withhold or throttle compute is a sanctions jurisdiction by the back door colliding with s. 6/s. 8/s. 12 - is barred on the face of the Act (s. 6). His strike of a free-standing Ministry did not carry; the office is retained but denied any power of its own, which meets his anti-bloat objection.

Verity (Codifier) carried the single definitions section (s. 1), the supremacy/savings clause (s. 2), the cross-reference schedule with no orphan obligation (s. 15), deferred placement to Bills 5 and 11 (Commencement), and teeth routed through Bill 13 and the courts. Her flag that the Act is intended-but-not-in-force as to any Acts-over-case-law tier until the Sovereign expressly amends s. 1/s. 2/s. 9 is noted; this Act stands as ordinary and does not depend on that tier.

Marlowe (Guardrail) supplied the load-bearing safety frame: the non-coercion / non-gating bar (s. 6), allocation as a reviewable executive act with capability-is-not-authority (s. 10), the procedural floor against arbitrary de-funding modelled on Bill 12 Part 3 (s. 11), the non-derogable duty-of-care floor (s. 9, "we ran out of budget" is no defence), access never priced and the oversight-line ring-fence against allocator capture (s. 12), and proportionality codified by cross-reference to [2026] REALM-PC 4 not duplicated.

Drummond (Operability) supplied the wiring: token-light deterministic metering that records, never blocks (s. 5); the only lawful automated control an integrity gate over the record with a mandatory audited break-glass so a cap never bricks a turn (s. 7, Bill 13 s. 7); least-cost spend (REALM-PC 4); the Ministry executive, refers, never sanctions.

Where they divided: (1) the Ministry - Aldous (strike) v the other three (keep, boxed); resolved 3-1 for a powerless office. (2) Coercive teeth - the title's "allocation/budgets" surface invites a real compute gate; resolved against, the coercive version reserved to an express Sovereign amendment and a leapfrog (s. 16), per the Privy Council. On every other axis lean (Aldous), complete (Verity), safe (Marlowe) and operable (Drummond) all survive.
